1.s: What is the main product formed when ethanol reacts with sodium?
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Ethanol reacts with sodium to give sodium ethoxide and hydrogen gas. Sodium acetate, ethanoic acid and ethyl acetate need oxidation or esterification instead.

1.s: Which of the following is not a Natural polymer?
1.x: Nylon was the first fully synthetic fibre (Carothers, 1935). Wool, silk and leather are natural protein polymers.

1.s: Which of the following is an example of colloidal solution of liquid in solid?
1.x: Cheese is a gel, a colloid of a liquid dispersed in a solid. Milk is an emulsion (liquid in liquid), mud a suspension and rubber a polymer.

1.s: Charcoal which is used in decolouring raw sugar is :
1.x: Animal (bone) charcoal is used to decolourise raw sugar in refining because it adsorbs the coloured impurities. Wood, sugar and coconut charcoal are not the standard answer.

1.s: Milk is an example of
1.x: Milk is an emulsion, fat droplets dispersed in water (oil-in-water). A gel is liquid in solid, a foam gas in liquid, and milk is not a suspension.

1.s: Select the incorrect statement out of the following :
o: Cotton is suitable for use as clothing in summer
Polycarbonate is used for making CDs
Acrylic is also called artificial silk as it is prepared
Teflon is used for coating non-stick kitchenwares
1.x: Rayon, made from wood-pulp cellulose, is called artificial silk; acrylic is 'artificial wool', so (c) is the incorrect statement. Cotton suits summer, polycarbonate makes CDs and Teflon coats non-stick pans.

1.s: The cleaning action of soap primarily depends on
o: Formation of micelles that trap grease and dirt
Conversion of soap into fatty acid anions in water
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Soap molecules form micelles: the oily tails trap grease and the ionic heads face water, so dirt washes away.

1.s: Which of the following materials is used to remove permanent hardness of water?
1.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
1.x: Sodium aluminium silicate (zeolite/permutit) removes permanent hardness by ion exchange of Ca/Mg for Na.

1.s: Why are tungsten filaments used in incandescent bulbs?
o: High specific resistance and high melting point
Low specific resistance and high melting point
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
1.x: Tungsten has high resistivity (heats up) and a very high melting point (3,422 °C), so the filament glows without melting.

1.s: What type of soap is generated when soap is dissolved in ethanol and then the surplus solvent is evaporated?
1.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
1.x: Dissolving soap in ethanol and evaporating the extra solvent gives transparent soap (NCERT Chemistry Class 12, 'Chemistry in Everyday Life').

1.s: The aromatic solvent widely used in the manufacturing of reinforced plastics and resins is ____.
1.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
1.x: Styrene is the aromatic monomer-solvent used with unsaturated polyester resins in reinforced plastics (fibreglass).

1.s: Which of the following Gas is produced when Baking soda is heated?
1.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
1.x: On heating, baking soda (NaHCO3) decomposes into sodium carbonate, water and carbon dioxide; the CO2 is what makes cakes rise. No CO, nitrogen or hydrogen is formed.

1.s: The wire in an electric iron is mainly made up of ____.
1.src: APPSC Sample Taker General Studies & Mental Abilities 2023
1.x: The heating element of an electric iron is nichrome (Ni-Cr alloy): high resistivity and a high melting point, and it does not oxidise when red-hot. Brass, bronze and steel are not heating-element materials.

1.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about the chemical process in baking a cake?

A. Baking soda is used to chemically leaven doughs and batters when it is mixed with an acid.

B. Cream of Tarter is one of the powdery acids used in baking powder to help leaven products.

C. Baking powder makes cakes rise by releasing carbon dioxide gas.
1.src: APPSC Executive Officer Gr-III Endowment Paper-I General Stu
1.x: All three are true: baking soda leavens when it meets an acid, cream of tartar (potassium bitartrate) is the dry acid in baking powder, and baking powder releases CO2 that makes the cake rise.

1.s: The Statute of Liberty in USA is Green in colour because of?
o: Every 30 years colour polish is applied
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
1.x: The copper skin of the Statue of Liberty oxidised (with CO2, moisture and sulphur compounds) into a green patina of basic copper carbonate. It is not paint and is not repolished.

1.s: Application of soap cleans dirty clothes through the process of
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
1.x: Soap molecules surround oily dirt and form micelles, an emulsion that is washed away by water. Soap lowers the surface tension of water, not of the dirt, and it forms no compound with dirt.

1.s: Which of the following materials is not a better absorber of sound compared to other given materials?
1.src: APPSC Royalty Inspector, Agriculture Officers, Town Planning
1.x: A hard, smooth steel sheet reflects sound; porous materials such as glass wool, polyvinyl foam and wood panels absorb it.

1.s: Which of the following materials has the highest melting point?
1.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
1.x: Tantalum carbide melts at about 3,880 °C, above tungsten (3,422 °C, the highest-melting metal). Glass and bauxite melt far lower.

1.s: Which of the following chemicals is normally used as 'anti freeze' in cars?
1.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
1.x: Ethylene glycol is mixed with radiator water as antifreeze: it lowers the freezing point. Hexane and benzene are not used, and ethyl alcohol evaporates too easily.

1.s: Which of the following salts does not contain water of crystallisation?
1.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
1.x: Baking soda (NaHCO3) has no water of crystallisation. Blue vitriol is CuSO4·5H2O, washing soda Na2CO3·10H2O and gypsum CaSO4·2H2O.

1.s: Sodium bicarbonate is the chemical name of which one of the following household items?
1.src: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer and Royalty Inspector in
1.x: Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3) is baking soda. Detergents are sulphonates, sanitisers are alcohol-based and talc is a magnesium silicate.

1.s:
Common salt besides being used in kitchen can also be used as the raw material for making the following:
i. Washing soda
ii. Bleaching powder
iii. Baking soda
iv. Slaked lime
1.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (i, ii and iii); it is added as option 5.
NCERT: common salt is the raw material for sodium hydroxide, baking soda, washing soda and bleaching powder (chlor-alkali process and Solvay process), so i, ii and iii. Slaked lime is made from limestone (CaCO3 → CaO → Ca(OH)2), so every printed code either omits a salt product or includes slaked lime.

1.s: Diamonds are crystals of?
1.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
1.x: Diamond is a crystalline form of pure carbon (each C bonded to four others). Quartz is silica, and glass is non-crystalline.

1.s: Type metal used to make printing types contains?
1.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
1.x: Type metal is an alloy of lead with antimony and tin (Pb + Sb + Sn); lead is the main metal. Steel, nickel and bismuth are not in it (bismuth is in Rose/Wood's metal).

1.s: Non-Stick Cookware is coated with
1.src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022
1.x: Non-stick pans are coated with PTFE (polytetrafluoroethylene, Teflon). PVC and polystyrene would melt or stick.

1.s: With what is non-stick kitchenware coated?
1.x: Non-stick kitchenware is coated with Teflon (polytetrafluoroethylene), a slippery, heat-resistant polymer. Graphite, silicon and glass are not non-stick coatings.

1.s: The Statue of Liberty is green because of
1.x: The Statue of Liberty is made of copper sheets, which oxidised over time into a green patina. It is not paint, algae or bronze.

1.s: The tubes used for dialysis and blood transfusion are made of
1.x: Dialysis and transfusion tubes and blood bags are made of PVC (poly vinyl chloride), which is flexible and can be sterilised.

1.s: Which kind of glass is used in the production of electric bulbs and optical instruments?
1.x: Flint (lead) glass has a high refractive index and dispersion, so it is used for lenses, prisms and electric bulbs. Pyrex is heat-resistant labware and hard glass is for chemical apparatus.

1.s: Milk of magnesia used as anti-acid is
1.x: Milk of magnesia is a suspension of magnesium hydroxide, Mg(OH)2, which neutralises excess stomach acid. The acetate, chloride and nitrate are not antacids.

1.s: Why is Sodium normally kept immersed in kerosene oil?
o: Kerosene oil is a good preservative
To prevent Sodium to absorb moisture in atmosphere
In open air Sodium explosively reacts with oxygen
1.x: NCERT: sodium reacts so vigorously that it catches fire in open air, so it is kept under kerosene. Avoiding moisture is part of the reason, but the vigorous reaction with oxygen is the answer the key gives.

1.s: PVC is a polymer used in a variety of applications in building and construction, health care, electronics, automobile and other sectors, in products ranging from piping and siding to blood bags and tubing. The full form of PVC is:
1.x: PVC stands for poly vinyl chloride, the polymer of vinyl chloride. The other expansions are not real polymers.

1.s: TEFLON is a polymer used for making non-stick cooking utensils. It is chemically known as:
1.x: Teflon is PTFE, polytetrafluoroethylene, the polymer of tetrafluoroethene (ethylene). The propylene, butylene and pentylene names are distractors.

1.s: Which materials are used for Superheater tubes?
1.x: Boiler superheater tubes are made of chromium-molybdenum (Cr-Mo) alloy steel, which keeps its strength and resists creep and oxidation at high temperature and pressure.

1.s: carats Gold contains by weight:
1.x: The stem means 22-carat gold: 22/24 = 91.6% gold, leaving about 8.4% of other metal such as copper.

1.s: Permanent hardness of water is due to the presence of:
1.x: Permanent hardness is due to sulphates and chlorides of calcium and magnesium (e.g. calcium sulphate). Bicarbonates cause temporary hardness, removed by boiling.

1.s: The element used in an electric filament is:
1.x: Bulb filaments are tungsten, which has the highest melting point of the metals (~3,420 °C). Aluminium and copper would melt, and propane is a gas.

1.s:
Which of the following statements are NOT true about gold?

a) soft metal

b) high density, 2.5x iron

c) pure gold ornaments cannot be made

d) not easily scratched

e) 18-carat gold has 25% copper
f) 1 carat = 100/24 percent
1.x: Untrue: (d) – gold is soft and easily scratched – and (c), since pure 24-carat ornaments can be made (they are merely soft). Gold's density (19.3) is about 2.5 times iron's (7.9), 18-carat gold has 25% other metal such as copper, and 1 carat = 100/24 %.

1.s: Some aircraft and car parts are made of the alloy 'dow metal'. What are the constituents of 'dow metal'?
1.x: Dow metal is a light magnesium alloy with a few per cent aluminium (Mg + Al), used in aircraft and car parts.

1.s: Baking soda is –
1.x: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate, NaHCO3. Sodium chloride is common salt and sodium hydroxide is caustic soda.

1.s: How much percentage of silver is found in German Silver?
1.x: German silver (nickel silver) is copper + zinc + nickel and contains no silver at all, so none of the percentages is right.

1.s: Phenol is used in the manufacture of which one of the following ?
1.x: Bakelite is made by condensing phenol with formaldehyde (Baekeland, 1907). PVC, nylon and polystyrene do not use phenol.

1.s: Bauxite, is an ore of which of the following metals?
1.x: Bauxite (hydrated aluminium oxide) is the main ore of aluminium. Iron ores are haematite and magnetite.

1.s:
Assertion (A) : Sodium metal is stored under kerosene.
Reason (R) : Metallic sodium melts when exposed to air.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not a correct
1.x: Sodium is stored under kerosene because it reacts violently with oxygen and moisture of the air, not because it melts in air; so A is true and R false.

1.s: Which of the following polymer is NOT a thermoplastic?
1.x: Neoprene (polychloroprene) is a synthetic rubber, an elastomer, not a thermoplastic. Teflon, polystyrene and polythene soften on heating and can be remoulded.

1.s:
Consider the following statements –
1. Anhydrous sodium carbonate is commonly known as baking soda.
2. Baking soda is used as a fire extinguisher.
3. Bleaching powder is produced in Hasenclever plant. Which of these statements is right :
1.x: Statement 1 is wrong: anhydrous Na2CO3 is soda ash (washing soda), while baking soda is NaHCO3. Baking soda is used in soda-acid fire extinguishers, and bleaching powder is made in the Hasenclever (or Bachmann) plant, so 2 and 3.

1.s: The chemical formula of baking soda is :
1.x: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate, NaHCO3. Na2CO3 is washing soda, CaCO3 limestone and Ca(OH)2 slaked lime.

1.s: Non-stick frying pans are coated with :
1.x: Non-stick frying pans are coated with Teflon (PTFE). Orlon is an acrylic fibre, and polystyrene and polypropylene are ordinary plastics.

1.s: The chemical used as a 'fixer' in photography is –
1.x: Hypo, sodium thiosulphate (Na2S2O3), is the photographic fixer: it dissolves the unexposed silver bromide. Sodium sulphate and borax are not fixers.

1.s: Teflon is a polymer of which of the following monomers?
1.x: Teflon (PTFE) is the polymer of tetrafluoroethylene. Vinyl chloride gives PVC and chloroprene gives neoprene.

1.s: Full form of PHBV biodegradable polymer:
o: Poly hydroxy butyric acid veratric acid
1.x: PHBV is poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate), a biodegradable copolymer of 3-hydroxybutanoic and 3-hydroxypentanoic acids.

1.s: The chemical formula of washing soda is :
1.x: Washing soda is sodium carbonate, Na2CO3 (as decahydrate). NaHCO3 is baking soda, NaOH caustic soda and Ca(OH)2 slaked lime.

1.s: The formula of baking soda is :
1.x: Baking soda is NaHCO3, sodium hydrogen carbonate. KHCO3 and K2CO3 are potassium salts and Na2CO3 is washing soda.

1.s:
With reference to Baking Soda, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It is Sodium hydrogen carbonate.
2. It is used in fire extinguishers.
Select the correct answer from the code given below:
Code :
1.x: Baking soda is sodium hydrogen carbonate (NaHCO3), and it is used in soda-acid fire extinguishers, where it releases CO2. Both statements are true.

1.s: Check these statements : (i) Brass is an alloy of Copper and Zinc. (ii) Magnetite is the main ore of Aluminium. (iii) Amalgams are that substances which mainly involve mercury. (iv) Potassium Nitrate (KNO3) is a chemical used in photography. Which of the above are true ? Code :
1.x: (i) Brass = copper + zinc and (iii) amalgams are mercury alloys are true. Magnetite (Fe3O4) is an iron ore, and photography uses silver bromide, not KNO3, so (i) and (iii).

1.s: Which chemical compound is present in Bleaching Powder?
1.x: Bleaching powder is calcium oxychloride, CaOCl2. Calcium hydroxide is only the slaked lime that is chlorinated to make it.

1.s: The important metal used with iron to produce stainless steel, is :
1.x: Stainless steel is iron alloyed with chromium (at least 10.5%, often with nickel); chromium's oxide film stops rusting. Carbon is in all steel, but it is not what makes it stainless.

1.s: Which one of the following polymers is used for making bullet-proof windows?
1.x: Bullet-resistant windows use tough, transparent polycarbonate laminated with glass. Polyurethane is used in foams and paints, polystyrene in packaging and polyamides in nylon fibres.

1.s: Solder used in soldering metal pieces is an alloy of :
1.x: Solder is a low-melting alloy of tin and lead. Bronze is tin + copper, and zinc is not in common solder.

1.s: Baking Soda is –
1.x: Baking soda is NaHCO3, sodium hydrogen carbonate. Sodium carbonate (Na2CO3) is washing soda.

1.s: Which one of the following materials contains calcium?
1.x: Gypsum is calcium sulphate dihydrate, CaSO4·2H2O. China clay (kaolin) and corundum contain aluminium, and talc is a magnesium silicate.

1.s: Baking soda is –
1.x: Baking soda is NaHCO3 (anhydrous). Na2CO3 is washing soda (decahydrate Na2CO3·10H2O), and the other formulae do not exist.

1.s: The important metal used with iron to make it rust free–
1.x: Chromium is alloyed with iron to make stainless steel, which resists rusting. Carbon is in all steel, but it does not stop rust.

1.s:
Consider the following statements :
1. Teflon and Dacron are polymers
2. Neoprene is synthetic rubber
3. Polythene is polyethylene polymer
4. Natural rubber is chloroprene
Which of the above statements are correct :
1.x: 1, 2 and 3 are true: Teflon and Dacron are polymers, neoprene is a synthetic rubber, and polythene is polyethylene. Natural rubber is polyisoprene, not chloroprene (that is neoprene).

1.s: Bakelite is formed by the condensation of :
1.x: Bakelite is formed by condensing phenol with formaldehyde. Urea-formaldehyde and melamine-formaldehyde are different resins.

1.s: What is untrue for bleaching powder?
o: It is more soluble in water
It is powder of light yellow colour
It releases chlorine after reaction with dilute acid
1.x: Bleaching powder is only partly soluble in water (it leaves a residue of lime), so 'more soluble' is the untrue claim. It is a pale-yellowish powder, an oxidant, and gives chlorine with dilute acid.

1.s: A polymer used for making nonstick surface coating for utensils is –
1.x: Teflon (PTFE) gives the non-stick coating of utensils. PVC, polystyrene and polypropylene are not non-stick and soften on heating.

1.s: Which one of the following polymers is used for the production of non-stick pans?
1.x: Teflon (PTFE) is the non-stick polymer used to coat pans. Neoprene is a synthetic rubber, PVC softens with heat, and gutta-percha is a natural latex.

1.s:
Consider the following statements : Hard water is not suitable for
1. Drinking
2. Washing clothes with soap
3. Use in boilers
4. Irrigating crops Which of these statements are correct ?
1.x:
Most books and keys: 1, 2, 3 and 4. Strictly: hard water is fit for drinking and is used in agriculture (PMF General Science Part 7 table: 'Domestic use ..., agriculture'); it is unsuitable mainly for washing with soap and for boilers, i.e. 2 and 3.
Hard water wastes soap (scum) and forms boiler scale, and books add drinking and irrigation, so the key is all four (1, 2, 3 and 4).

1.s: Stainless Steel is an alloy in which following is added along with iron:
1.x: Stainless steel is iron with chromium (plus some nickel), which makes it rust-resistant. Zinc is used for galvanising, tin for tin-plating.

1.s: The hair dye available in the market contains two bottles, one containing dye and other containing hydrogen peroxide. The bottles are mixed before applying the dye. The function of hydrogen peroxide is
o: to oxidise the dye to give desired colour.
to reduce the dye to give desired colour.
1.x: Hydrogen peroxide is an oxidising agent: it oxidises the dye precursors to develop the colour (and lightens natural pigment). It does not dilute, reduce or acidify the dye.

1.s: The advantage of detergents over soaps is
o: detergents could not give much lather.
detergents give lather even with hard water.
soaps give lather with only soft water.
1.x: Detergents form no scum with calcium and magnesium ions, so they lather even in hard water, which soaps cannot. Soap also dissolves in water, so 'soluble' is no advantage.

1.s: Soaps clean surfaces on the principle of based on
1.x: Soap cleans by lowering the surface tension of water, so it wets the surface and lifts grease into micelles. Viscosity, floatation and elasticity are not the principle.

1.s: Soaps clean surface on the principle is based on
1.x: Soap cleans by lowering the surface tension of water, so it wets the surface and lifts grease into micelles. Viscosity, floatation and elasticity are not the principle.

1.s:
Which of the following are fabrics that may contain polyester ?

I. Polycot
II. Polywool

III. Terrycot
1.x: Polycot (polyester + cotton), polywool (polyester + wool) and terrycot (terylene polyester + cotton) are all polyester blends.

1.s:
Which of the following statements are correct?

I. The soap molecules form structures called micelles.

II. Soap micelles cannot scatter light.

III. Only dirt gets collected in the centre of the micelle.
1.x: Soap molecules form micelles, and the oily dirt collects in the centre of the micelle (NCERT), so I and III. Micelles are colloid-sized and do scatter light, so II is wrong.

1.s: Cement is made hard with
1.x: Cement sets and hardens by hydration: its silicates and aluminates react with water to form hydrated gels and crystals. The key's wording 'hydration and dissociation of water' is the printed answer.

1.s: Brightness of the bulb decreases gradually with its period of use because of
o: evaporation of metal from filament of bulb.
decrease in electric supply to the bulb.
1.x: The hot tungsten filament slowly evaporates (sublimes), so it thins and the metal blackens the glass, and the bulb dims. Resistance actually rises as the filament thins.

1.s: Which of the following metal (shown by its symbol) is generally used for making filaments of bulb?
1.x: Tungsten (W) has the highest melting point of the metals, so it is used for bulb filaments. Fe is iron and Ag silver.

1.s: Which one of the following is used in the preparation of antiseptic solution?
1.x: Iodine (tincture of iodine, iodine in alcohol) is a standard antiseptic. Potassium nitrate, potassium chloride and iodine chloride are not.

1.s: What is the product formed when sodium bicarbonate is heated strongly?
1.x: On strong heating, sodium bicarbonate decomposes into sodium carbonate, water and CO2 (2NaHCO3 → Na2CO3 + H2O + CO2).

1.s: Which of the following is the chemical name of baking soda?
1.x: Baking soda is NaHCO3, sodium hydrogen carbonate. Sodium carbonate is washing soda.

1.s: What is the chemical name of slaked lime?
1.x: Slaked lime is calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)2, made by adding water to quicklime (CaO).

1.s: Which one among the following chemicals is used as washing soda?
1.x: Washing soda is sodium carbonate, Na2CO3·10H2O. Sodium bicarbonate is baking soda.

1.s: Which of the following properties is true for a tooth paste?
o: It is made up of Calcium phosphate, the material of tooth enamel.
1.x: Toothpaste is basic (alkaline) and neutralises the acid made by mouth bacteria, preventing tooth decay. Enamel is calcium phosphate, but toothpaste is not made of it.

1.s: A sample of ‘soft soap’ contains
1.x: Soft soaps are potassium salts of fatty acids (made with KOH); hard soaps are sodium soaps.

1.s: Which of the following is slaked lime?
1.x: Slaked lime is calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)2. CaO is quicklime, CaCO3 limestone and CaCl2 calcium chloride.

1.s: Which of the following is not correct about baking soda?
o: It is used in soda-acid fire extinguisher.
It is added for faster cooking.
It neutralises excess acid in the stomach.
1.x: Baking soda is a mild, non-corrosive base, so 'corrosive base' is the wrong statement. It is used in soda-acid extinguishers, added for faster cooking and as an antacid.

1.s: Soap solution used for cleaning purpose appears cloudy. This is due to the fact that soap micelles can
1.x: Soap micelles are colloid-sized and scatter light (Tyndall effect), so soap solution looks cloudy.

1.s: A fuse wire is made of
o: an alloy of tin and copper.
an alloy of tin and lead.
an alloy of tin and aluminium.
an alloy of nickel and chromium.
1.x: Fuse wire is a tin-lead alloy, which has a low melting point. Nichrome is for heater coils.

1.s: Filament in traditional incandescent bulb is made up of which metal?
1.x: The filament of an incandescent bulb is tungsten, which has the highest melting point of the metals.

1.s: Tungsten is used for the construction of filament in electric bulb because of its
1.x: Tungsten's very high melting point (~3,420 °C) lets the filament glow white-hot without melting.

1.s: The material used in electric heater is
1.x: Electric heaters use nichrome coils (high resistivity, high melting point, no oxidation). Tungsten is used for bulb filaments.

1.s: The coil wire in the electric room heater or electric cooking heater is called ……… .
1.x: The nichrome coil of a heater is called the heating element. 'Filament' is the word for a bulb's wire.

1.s: Which one of the following is used as an anti-freezer, which effectively depresses the freezing point of water in an automobile ?
1.x: Ethylene glycol is added to radiator water as antifreeze because it depresses the freezing point of water.

1.s: When items of jewellery made of metals such as copper or nickel are placed in a solution having a salt of gold, a thin film of gold is deposited by
1.x: A thin film of gold is deposited by electroplating: an electric current is passed through the gold salt solution with the jewellery as the cathode.

1.s: Sodium calcium silicate is called .......
1.x: Sodium calcium silicate is soft (soda-lime) glass. Hard glass is potassium calcium silicate; borosilicate (Jena/Pyrex) contains boron.

1.s: What is the dominant chemical present in detergent powder?
1.x:
Official key / most books: sodium carbonate (the main builder in detergent powder). Strictly: the cleansing agent of a detergent is the surfactant, a sodium alkyl sulphate / alkylbenzene sulphonate (NextGen Rocket Chemistry).
Answer keys take sodium carbonate, the builder that makes up most of a detergent powder by weight. Calcium carbonate is only a filler and HCl is never used.

1.s: What is the common name of CaOCl 2 ?
1.x: CaOCl2 (calcium oxychloride) is bleaching powder. Baking soda is NaHCO3 and washing soda Na2CO3.

1.s:
Match
List I with
List II.
List I
List II

A. German silver
1. Tin

B. Solder
2. Nickel

C. Bleaching powder
3. Sodium

D. Hypo
4. Chlorine
Codes A B C D A B C D
1.x: German silver contains nickel (A-2), solder tin (B-1), bleaching powder chlorine (C-4) and hypo is sodium thiosulphate (D-3), giving 2 1 4 3.

1.s: Which are the materials generally employed as solder in soldering operation in electronics?
1.x: Electronic solder is a tin-lead alloy (now often lead-free tin alloys). Iron and aluminium are not used.

1.s: Which alloy has bismuth, lead and tin?
1.x: Rose metal is a low-melting alloy of bismuth, lead and tin. Solder has only tin and lead, bell metal is copper + tin and German silver copper + zinc + nickel.

1.s: Bronze is often used to make statues and medals whereas brass is used in making utensils, scientific apparatus and cartridges. Both brass and bronze are copper containing alloys, yet they differ in their chemical composition for additionally containing.
o: zinc in brass and tin in bronze.
chromium in brass and nickel in bronze.
nickel in brass and tin in bronze.
iron in brass and nickel in bronze.
1.x: Brass is copper + zinc and bronze is copper + tin.

1.s: Natural rubber is a polymer of
1.x: Natural rubber is cis-polyisoprene, a polymer of isoprene. Styrene gives polystyrene and propene polypropylene.

1.s: Soap, removes grease by
1.x: Soap removes grease by emulsification: micelles break the grease into tiny droplets that stay dispersed in water and are rinsed away.

1.s: Soap helps in better cleaning of clothes because
o: it reduces the surface tension of solution.
1.x: Soap lowers the surface tension of water, so it wets the fabric and lifts dirt better. It is not a catalyst and does not absorb dirt.

1.s: Which of the following statements is not true for soap?
o: Soaps cannot be used in acidic medium.
Soaps form a white curdy precipitate with hard water.
Soaps are relatively stronger in their cleaning action than synthetic detergents.
1.x: Soaps are biodegradable, fail in acidic water and form a curdy scum with hard water, so the untrue claim is that soaps clean more strongly than synthetic detergents.

1.s: Which one of the following types of glasses is used for making optical instruments?
1.x: Flint (lead) glass, with its high refractive index and dispersion, is used for lenses and prisms of optical instruments. Pyrex is used for labware and soft glass for windows and bottles.

1.s: Which one of the following statements about glass is not correct?
o: Glass is often said to be a supercooled liquid.
Glass has no definite melting point.
Soda glass is harder than pyrex glass.
Boron is present in pyrex glass.
1.x: Pyrex (borosilicate, contains boron) is harder and more heat-resistant than soda glass, so 'soda glass is harder than Pyrex' is the incorrect statement. Glass is a supercooled liquid with no definite melting point.

1.s:
Consider the following statements.

I. Glass wool has tensile strength greater than steel.

II. Glass wool is fire proof.

III. Glass wool has high electrical conductivity and absorbs moisture.

IV. Glass wool is used to prepare fibre glass.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
1.x: Glass wool (fine glass fibres) has very high tensile strength, is fireproof and is used to make fibre glass. It is an electrical insulator and does not absorb moisture, so III is wrong.

1.s: What is full form of PVC?
1.x: PVC is poly vinyl chloride, the polymer of vinyl chloride.

1.s: Iodine can be separated from a mixture of iodine and potassium chloride by
1.x: Iodine sublimes on heating while KCl does not, so sublimation separates them. Filtration and sedimentation only work for insoluble solids and distillation for liquids.

1.s:
Which of the following is an example of sublimation?

I. Dry ice

II. Camphor

III. Ice
1.x: Dry ice (solid CO2) and camphor change directly from solid to gas, so they sublime. Ice melts to liquid water, so it is not an example.

1.s: The pH of water at 25° C is 7. When it is heated to 100° C, the pH of water
o: decreases up to 50° C and then increases
1.x: On heating, water ionises more, so [H+] increases and pH falls below 7 (about 6.1 at 100°C), although the water stays neutral.

1.s: Which is a natural colloid?
1.x: Blood is a natural colloid in which proteins and cells are dispersed in plasma. Urea, cane sugar and sodium chloride dissolve to form true solutions, not colloids.

1.s: Glycol is added to aviation gasoline because it
1.x: Glycol (ethylene glycol type) is an anti-freeze additive. It lowers the freezing point of aviation fuel at high altitude, so the petrol does not freeze.

1.s: Which one of the following salts when dissolved in water makes the solution basic?
1.x: Sodium acetate is a salt of a strong base (NaOH) and a weak acid (acetic acid). Its acetate ion hydrolyses to give OH-, so the solution is basic. NaCl is neutral; CuSO4 and FeCl3 are acidic.

1.s: Which chemical was an important symbol in our struggle for freedom?
1.x: Salt (sodium chloride) was the symbol of the freedom struggle through Gandhi's Dandi March and Salt Satyagraha (1930) against the salt tax.

1.s: Which one of the following is used as a mordant in dyeing and tanning industry?
1.x: Magnesium sulphate is used as a mordant in the dyeing and tanning industry. The other magnesium compounds are not used for this purpose.

1.s: Suppose you have four test tubes labelled as ‘A’, ‘B’, ‘C’ and ‘D’. ‘A’ contains plain water, ‘B’ contains solution of an alkali, ‘C’ contains solution of an acid, and ‘D’ contains solution of sodium chloride. Which one of these solutions will turn phenolphthalein solution pink?
1.x: Phenolphthalein turns pink in basic (alkaline) solution. Tube B has an alkali, while water, acid and NaCl solution are neutral or acidic and leave it colourless.

1.s: Which one among the following is not a property of salt?
o: Salts have ordered packing arrangements called lattices.
Salts have low melting points but high boiling points.
Salts conduct electricity when dissolved in water or even in the molten state.
1.x: Salts are ionic compounds with strong ionic bonds, so they have high melting and high boiling points. The statement that they have low melting points is false.

1.s: ………… is one of the most important technique for the separation of a mixture by passing it in solution or suspension through a medium in which the components move at different rates.
1.x: Chromatography separates mixture components because they move at different rates through a medium (stationary phase) carried by a solvent. Filtration, distillation and evaporation do not work this way.

1.s: Which of the following compounds is used as drying agent?
1.x:
Most keys: calcium oxide. Strictly: anhydrous calcium chloride is also a common drying agent, so two options fit (NCERT Class 11 Chemistry).
Calcium oxide (quicklime) absorbs water readily and is used as a drying agent, e.g. for ammonia gas. Gypsum and calcium hydroxide are not drying agents.

1.s: Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
1.x: Non-metal oxides such as CO2 and SO2 are acidic, forming acids with water. Metal oxides are generally basic.

1.s: Which one among the following contains the most neutrons?
1.x: Neutrons = mass number minus atomic number. Fe-59: 33; Cu-61: 32; Zn-61: 31; Zn-60: 30. So Fe-59 has the most.

1.s: Which of the following cannot be beaten into Sheets?
1.x: Gold, silver and aluminium are malleable and can be beaten into sheets. Potassium is a soft, reactive alkali metal that is not beaten into sheets.

1.s: Which one of the following is an oxidation-reduction reaction?
1.x: In 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO, Mg is oxidised and O2 is reduced, so it is a redox reaction. The other options are neutralisation, combination and double displacement with no change in oxidation state.

1.s: Nitric acid does not react with
1.x: Gold is a noble metal that dissolves only in aqua regia (3 HCl : 1 HNO3), so nitric acid alone does not react with it. Copper, zinc and iron react.

1.s: The manufacturing of iron from iron ore involves the process of
1.x: Iron is extracted by reducing its oxide ore with coke, which acts as the reducing agent. So the process is reduction.

1.s: Bronze is an alloy of
1.x: Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin. Brass is copper and zinc.

1.s: Which of the following has the lowest melting point ?
1.x: Tin melts at about 232 °C, lower than lead (327 °C), zinc (420 °C) and silver (962 °C).

1.s: What is the chemical formula for Sodium Chloride (Salt)?
1.x: Common salt is sodium chloride, NaCl: one Na+ ion combined with one Cl- ion, so the formula has no subscripts.

1.s: An amalgam of metal has which other element?
1.x: An amalgam is an alloy of a metal with mercury (Hg), the only common liquid metal.

1.s: Which of the following metals is the most reactive metal?
1.x: In the reactivity series calcium lies far above zinc, iron and copper, so it is the most reactive of these.

1.s: Which of the following metal is the heaviest?
1.x: Osmium is the densest naturally occurring metal, denser than iron, silver and nickel.

1.s: Which one among the following metals is used in fireworks to make a brilliant white light?
1.x: Magnesium burns with a dazzling white flame, so it is used in fireworks for brilliant white light. Sodium gives yellow.

1.s: Zinc is used to protect iron form corrosion because zinc is
o: a good conductor of heat and electricity.
1.x: Zinc is more electropositive (more reactive) than iron, so it corrodes in preference to iron and protects it (galvanisation, sacrificial protection).

1.s: Which is used in storage batteries?
1.x: Lead (lead-acid accumulators) is used in storage batteries, with lead plates in sulphuric acid.

1.s: Which among the following elements comes under metalloids?
1.x: Germanium is a metalloid (semiconductor) while zinc, silver and gold are true metals.

1.s: The solution of which one of the following will have pH less than 7?
1.x: FeCl3 is a salt of a strong acid (HCl) and a weak base Fe(OH)3, so it hydrolyses to give an acidic solution (pH<7). NaCl and KCl are neutral and NaOH is basic.

1.s: A copper substances when exposed to air gains a green coating due to the formation of
1.x: Copper exposed to moist air and CO2 slowly forms a green layer of basic copper carbonate, CuCO3·Cu(OH)2 (patina). CuO is black and the sulphate or nitrate do not form from air.

1.s: A substance acquired in the form of brownish film on a piece of iron left in the open for some time is
1.x: Iron exposed to air and moisture forms a brownish layer of hydrated iron oxide, called rust.

1.s: Which of the following is a natural fibre?
1.x: Silk is a natural protein fibre from silkworms. Rayon is semi-synthetic, and nylon and polyester are synthetic.

1.s: The number of angular and radial nodes for 4d orbital is respectively
1.x: For 4d, n=4 and l=2. Angular nodes = l = 2, and radial nodes = n-l-1 = 1.

1.s: Fabric made from ………does not get wrinkled easily.
1.x: Polyester is a synthetic fibre that resists wrinkling. Cotton, flax and silk crease easily.

1.s: Which of the following are amongst the few carbon-containing compounds not classified as organic?
1.x: Cyanides, along with oxides of carbon, carbonates and carbides, are carbon compounds traditionally treated as inorganic. Methane, propane and nucleic acids are organic.

1.s: Very small insoluble particles in a liquid may be separated it by using
1.x: Centrifugation spins the liquid so that very fine insoluble particles settle out. Decantation works only for larger particles that settle on their own.

1.s: What is formed when Magnesium is burnt?
1.x: Magnesium burns in air to form magnesium oxide, a white ash. It does not form baking soda, calcium carbonate or vinegar.

1.s: Which one of the following gives the highest amount of hydrogen ions (H+)?
1.x: Gastric juice contains HCl (pH ~1.5-3.5), so it is the most acidic and has the highest H+ concentration; lemon juice is a weaker acid and the others are basic.

1.s: Which of the following acids is present in ant bites?
1.x: Ant bites inject formic acid (methanoic acid), as the notes state.

1.s: In the reaction between hydrogen sulphate ion and water HSO4− + H2O → H3O+ + SO42−, the water acts as
1.x: Water accepts a proton from HSO4- to form H3O+, so water acts as a Bronsted-Lowry base.

1.s: Which one of the following could be the melting point of iron ?
1.x: Iron is a solid with a high melting point of about 1538°C, so 1500°C is the only option close to it.

1.s: A combustible gas is liberated when caustic soda solution is heated with
1.x: Zinc reacts with hot NaOH to give sodium zincate and hydrogen gas, which is combustible. NH4Cl would give ammonia, which is not combustible.

1.s: Which one of the following is the number of water molecules that share with two formula unit in Plaster of Paris?
1.x: Plaster of Paris is CaSO4·½H2O, i.e. (CaSO4)2·H2O, so two formula units share one water molecule.

1.s: What is detergent?
1.x: A detergent is a cleansing (purifying) agent that removes dirt and grease even in hard water, so 'refining agent' is the intended answer. It is not soap (detergents are soap substitutes), a medicine or a catalyst.

1.s: Which of the following is used to make light weight, but strong plastic ?
1.x: Methyl methacrylate polymerises to PMMA (perspex, acrylic glass), a light but strong, shatter-resistant plastic. Nylon is a fibre, polythene is soft, and PVC is heavier.

1.s: Which of the following is used to remove the green colour from glass?
1.x: Manganese dioxide ('glassmaker's soap') is added to glass to remove the green tint of ferrous iron. SiO2 is the glass itself, TiO2 a white pigment and SO2 a gas.

1.s: The Soda-acid fire extinguisher contains
o: sulphuric acid and solution of sodium hydrogen carbonate.
nitric acid and solution of sodium hydrogen carbonate.
sulphuric acid and solution of sodium carbonate.
sulphuric acid and solution of potassium carbonate.
1.x: A soda-acid extinguisher holds sulphuric acid and sodium hydrogen carbonate (baking soda) solution, which react to release CO2. Nitric acid, sodium carbonate or potassium carbonate are not used.

1.s: Which one of the following is used for water softening?
1.x: Calgon (sodium hexametaphosphate, Na6P6O18) softens permanent hard water. Mg(HCO3)2 causes hardness, and the other phosphates are not water softeners.

1.s: Nail polish remover contains
1.x: Nail polish remover is mainly acetone, a volatile solvent. Benzene, formaldehyde and acetic acid are not used for this.

1.s: Antacids are commonly used to get rid of acidity in the stomach. A commonly used antacid is
1.x: Milk of magnesia, Mg(OH)2, is a common mild antacid. Calcium hydroxide is too caustic, and the others are not antacids.

1.s: Which one of the following is used in the manufacture of soaps?
1.x: Soap is made by saponification of vegetable oils or animal fats with alkali (NaOH/KOH). Mobil, kerosene and cutting oils are petroleum (mineral) oils, which cannot be saponified.

1.s: Which one of the following elements is alloyed with iron to produce steel which can resist high temperatures and also have high hardness and abrasion resistance?
1.x: Tungsten is alloyed with iron to make tungsten (high-speed tool) steel that keeps its hardness at high temperatures and resists abrasion. Chromium mainly gives corrosion resistance (stainless steel) and nickel toughness.

1.s:
Which statements are correct?

I. In early 1930’s Nylon was prepared from coal, water and air.

II. Nylon was the first synthetic fibre.

III. Nylon fibre was strong elastic and light.
1.x: NCERT: nylon, the first fully synthetic fibre, was prepared in the 1930s from coal, water and air; it is strong, elastic and light. All three statements are correct.

1.s:
Match
List I with
List II and select the correct answer from the codes given below.
List I
List II

A. Morphine
1. Antiseptic

B. Sodium
2. Alloy

C. Boric acid
3. Analgesic

D. German silver
4. Kerosene oil
Codes A B C D A B C D
1.x: Morphine is an analgesic (3), sodium is stored in kerosene (4), boric acid is an antiseptic (1) and German silver is an alloy (2), giving 3-4-1-2.

1.s: What is deposited on iron in the process of galvanisation?
1.x: Galvanisation coats iron with zinc to prevent rusting. Tin plating is a different process.

1.s:
Consider the following statements.

I. Photochromic lenses are lenses that darken on exposure to ultraviolet light.

II. Photochromic properties is due to embedded microcrystalline of silver chloride in the glass.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
1.x: Photochromic lenses darken in UV light because of microcrystals of silver halide (silver chloride) embedded in the glass, so both statements are correct.

1.s:
Assertion (A) Cellulose is used in making shatter-proof glass.
Reason (R) Polysaccharides are not soluble in water.
Codes
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
1.x: Cellulose derivatives (cellulose acetate/nitrate) formed the plastic interlayer in early shatter-proof (safety) glass, and polysaccharides such as cellulose are insoluble in water, but insolubility is not why it is used. Both true, R not the explanation.

1.s: Which one of the following is used in making Bullet proof Jacket’?
1.x: Body armour has used layered glass-fibre (fibrous glass) and aramid fibres; laminated glass is rigid bullet-resistant glazing for windows, not a jacket. Gun metal and lead are too heavy.

1.s:
When hard water is evaporated completely the white solid remains in the container. It may be due to the presence of

I. Carbonates of Ca and Mg.

II. Sulphates of Ca and Mg.

III. Chlorides of Ca and Mg.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
1.x: Hard water carries Ca and Mg bicarbonates (which become carbonates on heating), sulphates and chlorides; all of them stay as a white residue when the water evaporates.

1.s: Which pair of following is of Copper alloys?
1.x: Brass (Cu + Zn) and bronze (Cu + Sn) are copper alloys. Invar is iron-nickel and nichrome is nickel-chromium.

1.s:
: Which of the following is a correct match of chemical compounds and their uses? Chemical Compound
I. Analgesics
II. Antibiotics
III. Antiseptics
o: I.c II.a III.b Use a. To treat infections b. To prevent the growth of microorganisms c. To reduce or abolish pain
1.x: Analgesics reduce pain (c), antibiotics treat infections (a), and antiseptics prevent the growth of microorganisms on living tissue (b).

1.s: Chemically, baking soda is
1.x: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3). Baker's yeast is a fungus, and sodium chloride is common salt.

1.s: Chemically, baking soda is
1.x: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3). Baker's yeast is a fungus, and sodium chloride is common salt.

1.s: The ions present in hard water are
1.x: Hard water contains dissolved calcium and magnesium salts; their Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions form scum with soap.

1.s: Which of the following is a chemical reaction?
o: Ice melting in a glass of lemonade
An aluminium vessel melting at very high heat
Bleaching changing the colour of a T-shirt
1.x: Bleaching changes the colour by a chemical (oxidation) reaction. Melting ice, a melting aluminium vessel and solidifying coconut oil are physical changes of state.

1.s: The nonstick pans used in Kitchens are coated with:
1.x: Non-stick pans are coated with polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE, Teflon). PVC, polyethylene and polyamide (nylon) are not.

1.s: Which type of chemical reaction is involved when baking soda is added to vinegar?
1.src: APPSC 2023 Lecturers in Government Degree Colleges
1.x: Baking soda (a base) reacts with the acetic acid of vinegar in an acid-base (neutralisation) reaction that releases CO2.

1.s: Which one of the following substances is used in photography and also as an antichlor ?
1.x: Sodium thiosulphate (hypo) is the photographic fixer and also an antichlor (removes excess chlorine).

1.s: Doctors, Artists and Sculptors use Calcium Sulphate which is popularly known as –
1.x: Calcium sulphate hemihydrate is Plaster of Paris, used by doctors for casts and by artists and sculptors. Quicklime is CaO and limestone CaCO3.

1.s: Which of the following is an example of a non-cellulosic fibre?
1.x: Rayon, linen and jute are made of cellulose; nylon is a synthetic polyamide, a non-cellulosic fibre.

1.s: Which of the following cannot be put out with water?
o: Fires that rise with an explosion
1.x: Water is not used on oil fires: oil floats on water and the burning oil spreads. Such fires are put out with foam, CO2 or sand.

1.s:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as
Assertion (A) and the other as
Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : A solution of table salt in a glass of water is homogeneous.
Reason (R) : A solution having different compositions throughout is homogeneous.
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct
1.x: Salt dissolved in water is a homogeneous solution (A true). A homogeneous solution has the same composition throughout, so R is false.

1.s: Which of the following are the constituents of a soda acid fire extinguisher ?
o: Conc. Sulfuric acid and aluminium sulphate
Dil. Sulfuric acid and sodium carbonate
Dil. Sulfuric acid and sodium bicarbonate solution
Conc. Sulfuric acid and sodium carbonate solution
1.x: A soda-acid extinguisher holds sodium bicarbonate solution and sulphuric acid, which react to give CO2. Aluminium sulphate is used in foam extinguishers, and sodium carbonate is not the usual charge.

1.s: The gas used in fire extinguishers is
1.x: CO2 is used in fire extinguishers because it does not burn and cuts off the oxygen supply. Hydrogen burns, and SO2 and H2S are toxic.

1.s: Washing soap produces a scum with hard water and not much foam because the hard water contains
1.x: Hard water has dissolved inorganic salts of calcium and magnesium, which form insoluble scum with soap instead of lather.

1.s:
Assertion (A) : Phenyl is used as a household germicide.
Reason (R) : Phenyl is phenol derivative and phenol is an effective germicide.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
1.x: Phenyl (phenol-derived disinfectant) is used as a household germicide because phenol is an effective germicide. Both true and R explains A.

1.s: Bullet-proof vests are made from a fabric of
1.x: Bullet-proof vests are made of tightly woven high-strength synthetic polyamide fibres, nylon (ballistic nylon) and the aramid Kevlar. Jute and cotton are too weak, and steel wire is not a fabric.

1.s: Which of the following is a super cooled liquid?
1.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
1.x: Glass is an amorphous solid often called a supercooled liquid. Ice cream, coke and liquid nitrogen are not.

1.s: What is the phenomenon of the scattering of light as a light beam passes through a colloid called?
1.src: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer and Royalty Inspector in
1.x: The Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by colloidal particles; true solutions show none.

1.s: Which of the following is a super cooled liquid?
1.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
1.x: Glass is an amorphous solid often called a supercooled liquid. Ice cream, gelatine and helium are not.

1.s: ' Chiral ' in Greek represents
1.x: 'Chiral' comes from the Greek 'kheir' = hand: a chiral molecule is not superimposable on its mirror image, like left and right hands.

1.s: Because of impurities the boiling point of a liquid –
1.x: Dissolved impurities raise the boiling point of a liquid (elevation of boiling point).

1.s: On adding common salt to water, the boiling point and freezing point of water will :
1.x: A dissolved solute such as salt raises the boiling point (elevation) and lowers the freezing point (depression) of water. So boiling point increases and freezing point decreases.

1.s: Which one of the following changes occurs when salt is added into the water?
o: Boiling point is increased and freezing point decreased
Boiling point is decreased and freezing point is
Both boiling point and freezing point are decreased
Both boiling point and freezing point are increased
1.x: Salt raises the boiling point and lowers the freezing point of water (colligative properties).

1.s: Who discovered the rubber making process through the vulcanisation method ?
1.x: Charles Goodyear (1839) discovered vulcanisation – heating rubber with sulphur to make it hard and elastic. Dunlop made the pneumatic tyre.

1.s: Who among the following proposed that atom is indivisible?
1.x: Dalton's atomic theory (1808) held that atoms are indivisible. Rutherford found the nucleus; Avogadro dealt with molecules in gases.

1.s: Which one among the following is not a chemical change?
1.x: Evaporation of water is a physical change (no new substance). Curdling, ripening and burning make new substances – chemical changes.

1.s: The passage of an electric current through a conducting liquid causes … .
1.x: Current through a conducting liquid (electrolyte) decomposes it – a chemical reaction (electrolysis, electroplating).

1.s: Through the reaction of benzene and chlorine in the presence of catalyst say iron. Which of the following would be obtained?
1.x: Benzene + Cl2 with iron (FeCl3) catalyst undergoes electrophilic substitution to give chlorobenzene. Benzene hexachloride needs UV light (addition).

1.s:
Statement I All compounds contain more than one element. Statement II All compounds are heterogeneous mixtures.
Codes
o: Both the statements are individually true and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I.
Both the statements are individually true but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I.
Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
1.x: Every compound has two or more elements chemically combined (I true), but compounds are pure, homogeneous substances, not heterogeneous mixtures (II false).

1.s:
Statement I Glass is not considered as a true compound. Statement II Glass does not have a definite melting point.
Codes
o: Both the statements are individually true and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I.
Both the statements are individually true, but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I.
Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
1.x: Glass is an amorphous mixture of silicates (a supercooled liquid), so it is not a true compound and has no sharp melting point – the printed key takes II as the reason for I.

1.s: A thick paste of cement, sand and water is called
1.x: Cement + sand + water paste = mortar; concrete also has gravel, and RCC has steel bars.

1.s: Which of the following is a major component of German silver?
1.x: German silver is copper (~60%) + zinc + nickel; it has no silver. Copper is the major component.

1.s: What are the maximum numbers of electrons that can be present in a shell represented by shell number ‘n’?
1.x: Maximum electrons in shell n = 2n² (K 2, L 8, M 18, N 32).

1.s:
An acid is a substance which

I. is sour in taste.

II. turns red litmus paper into blue.
1.x: Acids are sour and turn blue litmus red; turning red litmus blue is a property of bases, so only I is correct.

1.s: Which of the following is an aldehyde?
1.x: The suffix '-al' marks an aldehyde: propanal (CH3CH2CHO). Propanol is an alcohol, propanone a ketone, propyne an alkyne.

1.s: The oxidation number of nickel in K4[Ni(CN)4] is
1.x: In K4[Ni(CN)4]: 4(+1) + x + 4(−1) = 0, so x = 0 – nickel is in the zero oxidation state.

1.s: Which one of the following oxides dissolves in water?
1.x: Na2O is a basic alkali-metal oxide that dissolves in water to form NaOH. CuO, Al2O3 and Fe2O3 are insoluble.

1.s: If formula of sodium salt of an anion X is Na 2X , then the formula of its aluminium salt would be
1.x: Na2X means X has valency 2 (X²⁻); with Al³⁺ the neutral formula is Al2X3.

1.s: According to which one of the following laws it is indicated that when two or more gases react with one another, their volumes bear a simple ratio?
1.x: Gay-Lussac's law of combining volumes: reacting gases and gaseous products bear simple whole-number volume ratios.

1.s: Which of the following is a heterogeneous mixture?
1.x: A suspension (e.g. muddy water) is a heterogeneous mixture; a solution is homogeneous.

1.s: Silver ware turns black after a period of time due to the formation of
1.x: Silver reacts with hydrogen sulphide in the air to form black silver sulphide (Ag2S) – tarnishing.

1.s: How many elements are there in the 5th Period of Modern Periodic Table?
1.x: The 5th period (Rb to Xe) has 18 elements; periods 2–3 have 8, 4–5 have 18, 6–7 have 32.

1.s: JJ Thomson’s proposed model of atom is generally called ………… model.
1.x: J.J. Thomson's atom – electrons embedded in a positive sphere – is the plum-pudding model.

1.s: The atomic weights are expressed in terms of atomic mass unit. Which one of the following is used as standard?
1.x: Atomic masses are expressed relative to carbon-12: 1 u = 1/12 the mass of a ¹²C atom (since 1961).

1.s: If we plot a graph between volume V and inverse of pressure p (i.e. 1/p) for an ideal gas at constant temperature T, the curve so obtained is a
1.x: Boyle's law V = k(1/p) at constant T, so V against 1/p is a straight line through the origin (V against p is a hyperbola).

1.s: Which of the following is the maximum number of electrons that can be present in M-shell?
1.x: The M shell is n = 3: 2n² = 18 electrons.

1.s: The number of maximum electrons in N shell is
1.x: The N shell is n = 4: 2n² = 32 electrons.

1.s: The bond which is present between water molecules is
1.x: Neighbouring water molecules are linked by hydrogen bonds, which give water its high boiling point. The O–H bonds within one molecule are covalent, not the bond between molecules.

1.s: Which one of the following is mono- atomic ?
1.x: Noble gases such as helium exist as single atoms. Hydrogen is diatomic (H2), phosphorus P4 and sulphur S8.

1.s: The proposition ‘equal volumes of different gases contain equal numbers of molecules at the same temperature and pressure’ is known as
1.x: Avogadro's hypothesis (1811) states that equal volumes of all gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules. Gay-Lussac's law is about combining volumes.

1.s: Which of the following is not a noble gas?
1.x: Hydrogen is a reactive non-metal, not a noble gas. Helium, neon and argon are noble gases with full outer shells, hence chemically unreactive.

1.s: Iron sheet kept in moist air covered with rust. Rust is
o: a mixture of iron and dust
a mixture of iron, oxygen and water
1.x: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, Fe2O3·xH2O, a chemical compound. It is not an element or a mere mixture.

1.s: Constantan is an alloy of copper and ......
1.x: Constantan is a copper-nickel alloy (about 55:45) with a nearly constant resistance. Tin, iron and aluminium are not its partners.

1.s: Which one of the following compounds does not exhibt a different oxidation number of the same element?
1.x: In Fe2O3 every iron is +3. Pb3O4 (Pb +2, +4), Fe3O4 (Fe +2, +3) and Mn3O4 (Mn +2, +3) are mixed-valence oxides.

1.s: Multiplication of equivalent weight and valency of an element is equal to …… .
1.x: Equivalent weight = atomic weight / valency, so equivalent weight × valency = atomic weight. Density and atomicity are unrelated.

1.s: The rusting of iron nail
o: does not affect weight but iron is oxidised.
does not affect weight but iron is reduced.
1.x: Rusting adds oxygen and water to iron (Fe2O3·xH2O), so the nail gains weight. Iron is oxidised, not reduced.

1.s: Which one of the following will not produce carbon dioxide on reacting with an aqueous solution of hydrochloric acid?
1.x: Limestone, chalk and marble are all CaCO3 and release CO2 with HCl. Quicklime (CaO) is an oxide, giving only CaCl2 and water.

1.s: Inert gases are
1.x: Inert (noble) gases have complete outer shells, so they are stable and chemically unreactive. They are not very active.

1.s:
Consider the following reaction. CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2 O
Which of the following about the reaction given above is/are correct?

I. Carbon is oxidised

II. Hydrogen is oxidised

III. Hydrogen is reduced

IV. Carbon is reduced
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
1.x: Carbon goes from −4 in CH4 to +4 in CO2, so it is oxidised. Hydrogen stays +1, so it is neither oxidised nor reduced; oxygen is reduced.

1.s: Ultra purification of a metal is done by :
1.x: Zone refining melts a narrow zone that carries impurities along, yielding ultra-pure metals. Smelting and leaching are extraction steps.

1.s:
Which of the following solutions will not change the colour of blue litmus paper to red?

I. Acid solution

II. Base solution

III. Common salt solution
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
1.x: Only acids turn blue litmus red. A base (blue stays blue) and neutral common salt solution do not change it.

1.s:
Which of the following is/are state function/functions ?

I. q + W
II. q
III.W
IV. H − TS
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
1.x: q + W equals ΔU, and H − TS is the Gibbs energy G, both state functions. Heat q and work W separately depend on the path.

1.s: White Phosphorus glows in the dark due to
1.x: White phosphorus slowly oxidises in air and the reaction gives off light (phosphorescence/chemiluminescence). It has a low, not high, ignition temperature.

1.s: In which one of the following is the valence electronic configuration, ns2 np 3 found?
1.x: Nitrogen (1s² 2s² 2p³) has the valence configuration ns² np³. Carbon is 2p², oxygen 2p⁴ and argon 3p⁶.

1.s: The pH of fresh ground water slightly decreases upon exposure to air because
o: carbon dioxide from air is dissolved in the water.
oxygen from air is dissolved in the water.
the dissolved carbon dioxide of the ground water escapes into air.
the dissolved oxygen of the ground water escapes into air.
1.x: CO2 from the air dissolves to form weak carbonic acid, lowering pH slightly. Dissolved oxygen does not change pH.

1.s: Rust needs three components to occur i.e. .........
1.x: Rusting needs iron, oxygen and moisture together. Nitrogen and helium play no part.

1.s: Which of the following elements is found in all organic compounds?
1.x: Organic compounds are by definition carbon compounds. Oxygen and nitrogen are in many but not all, and calcium is not typical.

1.s: The product of equivalent weight and valency of an element is equal to
1.x: Equivalent weight = atomic weight / valency, so equivalent weight × valency = atomic weight.

1.s: Which one of the following properties changes with valency?
1.x: Equivalent weight = atomic weight / valency, so it changes when an element shows a different valency. Atomic weight, molecular weight and density do not.

1.s: Under which condition real gas can work as an ideal gas?
1.x: At low pressure and high temperature molecules are far apart and fast, so attractions and molecular volume matter little and the gas behaves ideally.

1.s: Water is a good solvent. This is due to high
1.x: Water's high dielectric constant (about 80) weakens attraction between ions, so ionic compounds dissolve easily. Surface tension and specific heat are unrelated.

1.s: Which chemical law proposes that ‘soft drinks and soda bottles are sealed under high pressure to increase the solubility of CO2?
1.x: Henry's law says gas solubility in a liquid increases with the pressure of the gas, so CO2 is dissolved in soft drinks under high pressure.

1.s: Which one of the following types of glass can cut off ultraviolet rays?
1.x: Crookes glass contains cerium oxide and absorbs ultraviolet rays, so it is used in protective spectacles. Soda, Pyrex and Jena glass transmit UV.

1.s: Two electrons in an orbital are differentiated by which of the following?
1.x: Two electrons in the same orbital have the same n, l and m values and differ only in spin quantum number (+1/2 and -1/2), per the Pauli exclusion principle.

1.s: Tyndall effect is related to the ……… of light.
1.x: The Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by colloidal particles, which makes the beam's path visible.

1.s: ………are homogeneous mixtures of two or more components.
1.x: Solutions are homogeneous mixtures of two or more components; emulsions are colloids (heterogeneous), and enzymes are proteins.

1.s: An emulsion is a colloid of a
1.x: An emulsion is a colloid of one liquid dispersed in another liquid, e.g. milk (fat in water).

1.s: Glass is soluble in
1.x: Hydrofluoric acid reacts with the silica in glass to form silicon tetrafluoride, so it dissolves glass. The other acids do not.

1.s: A molecule of a substance is similar to its atom for
1.x: A monoatomic molecule consists of a single atom, so the molecule is the same as the atom, as in noble gases.

1.s: Phosphorus is kept in water because
o: its ignition temperature is very high.
its ignition temperature is very low.
1.x: White phosphorus has a very low ignition temperature and catches fire in air, so it is stored under water.

1.s: Which of the following is NOT an unsaturated carbon compound?
1.x: Butane is a saturated alkane (only single bonds), whereas acetylene, pentene and benzene contain double or triple bonds and are unsaturated.

1.s: Methyl propane is an isomer of
1.x: Methylpropane (isobutane) has formula C4H10, the same as n-butane but with a branched chain, so they are structural isomers.

1.s: The elements of group in the Periodic table
1.x: Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons and hence similar chemical properties.

1.s: Which one of the following is not a periodic property i.e., does not show any trend on moving from one side to the other in the Periodic Table?
1.x: Radioactivity depends on nuclear stability, not on electron arrangement, so it shows no periodic trend. Atomic size, valency and electronegativity vary periodically.

1.s: Which of the following is the symbol of the metal that occurs in liquid form at ordinary temperature?
1.x: Mercury (Hg) is the only metal that is liquid at ordinary temperature. K, Ag and Pb are solids.

1.s: Which of the following elements has the lowest melting point?
1.x: Radon is a noble gas with a very low melting point (about -71 C), far lower than sodium, tin or radium.

1.s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?

I. Metallic oxides are said to be basic oxides.

II. Non-metallic oxides are basic in nature.

III. All acids have similar chemical properties.
Codes
1.x: Metallic oxides are basic and all acids share similar properties (they give H+ ions), so I and III are correct. Non-metallic oxides are acidic, not basic, so II is false.

1.s: Which of the following is a sweet smelling substance?
1.x: Esters have sweet, fruity smells; ammonia is pungent and alcohols are not typically sweet-smelling.

1.s: Ammonia (NH3) obtained from different sources always has same proportion of nitrogen and hydrogen. It proves the validity of law of
1.x: A compound always has the same elemental proportion by mass regardless of source, which is the law of constant (definite) proportions.

1.s: Which one of the following is used for writing on glass?
1.x: Hydrogen fluoride attacks and etches glass (silicon dioxide), so it is used to write on glass; graphite and others do not.

1.s: Liquid water is denser than ice due to
1.x: Hydrogen bonding makes ice an open lattice, so ice is less dense than liquid water.

1.s: Which compound, when dissolved in water, conducts electricity and forms a basic solution?
1.x: NaOH is a strong base that dissociates into ions, conducting electricity and giving a basic solution; HCl and CH3COOH are acids, and CH3OH does not ionise.

1.s: To weld metals together, high temperature required such a high temperature is obtained by burning
1.x: The oxyacetylene flame (acetylene burning in oxygen) gives the highest flame temperature (~3000 C), used for welding; nitrogen does not support burning.

1.s: In a reaction, what is the loss of hydrogen by substance called as?
1.x: By the OIL RIG rule oxidation is loss (of electrons, and of hydrogen), so loss of hydrogen is oxidation, not reduction.

1.s: When a substance loses oxygen during a reaction, it is called … .
1.x: Loss of oxygen from a substance is reduction, the opposite of oxidation (gain of oxygen); corrosion is a different process.

1.s: When a spoon is to be electroplated with nickel the spoon is
o: dipped in a nickel sulphate solution.
made anode and a pure nickel rod, the cathode.
made cathode and a pure nickel red, the anode.
coated with nickel sulphate and dried.
1.x: In electroplating the object to be plated (the spoon) is made the cathode and the plating metal (pure nickel) is the anode, so nickel dissolves from the anode and deposits on the spoon.

1.s: The normal butane and isobutane are
1.x: n-Butane and isobutane share the formula C4H10 but differ in carbon chain (straight vs branched), so they are chain isomers.

1.s: Which of the following reaction is an example of exothermic reaction ?
o: The decomposition of vegetable matter into compost
1.x: Burning of natural gas, respiration and composting all release heat, so all are exothermic reactions.

1.s: Combustion of a candle is
1.x: Burning a candle is combustion, which releases heat and light, so it is exothermic. It is also a chemical change, not a physical one.

1.s: What is an endothermic reaction?
o: Reaction in which heat is released.
Reaction in which heat is absorbed.
Reaction in which neither heat is released nor absorbed.
1.x: An endothermic reaction absorbs heat from its surroundings, such as the decomposition of calcium carbonate on heating. A reaction that releases heat is exothermic.

1.s:
Following statements are made in connection with Carbon dioxide ( CO2 ).

I. CO2 is a poisonous gas.

II. CO2 is an acidic oxide.

III. CO2 turns lime water milky.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
1.x: CO2 is an acidic oxide (forms carbonic acid with water) and turns lime water milky due to calcium carbonate formation. It is not poisonous, only an asphyxiant at high concentration, so statement I is wrong.

1.s: Which of the following gas causes explosion in coal mines?
1.x: Methane (firedamp) mixes with air in coal mines and forms an explosive mixture; CO2 and nitrogen are not flammable.

1.s: In a periodic table, while moving from left to right in a period, number of remains same.
1.x: Moving left to right across a period, electrons and protons increase by one per element, but the number of shells (the period number) stays the same.

1.s: Which one of the following substances is not a mixture?
1.x: Ice is just solid water, a pure compound, so it is not a mixture; ice-cream, air and honey are mixtures of several components.

1.s: Which one of the following elements exists in liquid state at room temperature ?
1.x: Mercury is the only metal liquid at room temperature; lead, sodium and calcium are solids.

1.s: Which of the following metal remains in liquid form at room temperature?
1.x: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature; cadmium, germanium and tin are solids.

1.s: Which one of the following carbon compounds will not give a sooty flame?
1.x: Hexane is a saturated alkane with a low carbon percentage and burns with a clean flame. Benzene, naphthalene and anthracene are aromatic and carbon-rich, so they burn with a sooty flame.

1.s: Which one of the following reducing agents can also act as an oxidising agent?
1.x: SO2 has sulphur in the +4 state, so it can be oxidised to +6 or reduced to lower states and acts as both. H2 and HI act mainly as reducing agents, and H2S too.

1.s: The gas which turns lime water milky is
1.x: CO2 reacts with lime water (calcium hydroxide) to form insoluble calcium carbonate, which makes it milky.

1.s: Yellow colour of usual nitric acid is due to the presence of which one of the following?
1.x: Nitric acid decomposes in light to give brown NO2, which dissolves in the acid and gives it a yellow colour.

1.s: In which of the following pairs are the Isoelectronic ions?
1.x: Na+ and O2− both have 10 electrons, so they are isoelectronic. In the other pairs the electron counts differ.

1.s: Which one of the following is a reduction reaction?
1.x: In 2HgO → 2Hg + O2, mercury(II) oxide loses oxygen and Hg is reduced from +2 to 0. The other reactions are oxidation or combination reactions.

1.s: Which one of the following polymers is made of proteins ?
1.x: Wool is made of the protein keratin, whereas cotton and jute are cellulose and rubber is a hydrocarbon polymer.

1.s: Which of the following is the first man made plastic that is bad conductor of heat ?
1.x: Bakelite, made from phenol and formaldehyde, was the first fully synthetic plastic and is a poor conductor of heat and electricity, so it is used for handles and switches. Polythene, nylon and Teflon came later.

1.s: Which of the following has a strong fruity fragrance?
1.x: Ethyl acetate is an ester, and esters have sweet, fruity smells. Methyl chloride, methanoic acid and methanol do not smell fruity.

1.s: On exposure to moist air, copper gains a green coat on its surface due to formation of which one of the following compounds ?
1.x: In moist air copper reacts with CO2, oxygen and water to form a green coat of basic copper carbonate (the patina of the Statue of Liberty). Copper oxide is black and copper sulphate is blue.

1.s: In which among the following molecules is the distance between two adjacent carbon atoms largest?
1.x: Ethane has a C-C single bond (about 154 pm), longer than the double bond in ethene, the triple bond in ethyne or the intermediate bond in benzene.

1.s: Which one of the following is not a monoatomic element ?
1.x: Iodine exists as diatomic I2 molecules, whereas copper, helium and barium occur as single atoms (monoatomic).

1.s: Which one of the following is the hardest metal?
1.x: Among the options, tungsten is the hardest metal; it also has the highest melting point.

1.s: The substance that cannot be further decomposed by chemical means is
1.x: Silver is an element, so it cannot be split further by chemical means. Sugar and water are compounds and air is a mixture.

1.s: Laughing gas is
1.x: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is laughing gas, a mild anaesthetic. Nitric oxide is NO, and the other two are higher oxides.

1.s: Chemically Dry Ice is –
o: Mixture of ice and common salt
1.x: Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide, which sublimes without melting. It is not ice, a salt mixture or sulphur.

1.s: Which among the following is not a polymer ?
1.x: Caprolactam is the monomer from which nylon-6 is made, so it is not a polymer. Nylon, Teflon and polystyrene are polymers.

1.s: Which one of the following colours is supplied by Sodium Chromate?
1.x:
Official key / most books: Red. Strictly: sodium chromate is a yellow solid; the orange-red salt is sodium dichromate (Wikipedia, Sigma-Aldrich).
The UPPSC key and books give red for sodium chromate (Na2CrO4). Blue, green and black are not linked to it.

1.s: Which of the following is the main ingredient of cement?
1.x: Limestone (~75%) is the main ingredient of cement, with clay the smaller part. Gypsum is added only to slow setting.

1.s: Which of the following are exothermic processes ? (i) Evaporation of water. (ii) Dilution of an acid (H2SO4). (iii) Reaction of water with quick lime. (iv) Sublimation of camphor (crystals).
1.x: Diluting sulphuric acid and slaking quicklime with water both give out heat. Evaporation and sublimation absorb heat, so options with (i) or (iv) are wrong.

1.s: The pH value of distilled water exposed to air is?
1.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
1.x: Distilled water left open dissolves CO2 from the air and forms carbonic acid, so its pH falls slightly below 7. It is exactly 7 only when pure and sealed.

1.s: How many covalent bonds are present in a Chloropropane molecule having molecular formula C3H7Cl?
1.x: C3H7Cl has 2 C–C, 7 C–H and 1 C–Cl single bonds = 10 covalent bonds.

1.s: Silver gets corroded due to ……… in air.
1.x: Silver tarnishes black by reacting with hydrogen sulphide in air to form silver sulphide (Ag2S).

1.s: Regarding the atom of a chemical element, the magnetic quantum number refers to
1.x: The magnetic quantum number (m) gives the orientation of an orbital in space; shape = azimuthal (l), size = principal (n), spin = s.

1.s: Which one of the following materials is very hard and very ductile?
1.x: Tungsten is very hard yet ductile enough to be drawn into bulb filaments. Carborundum and cast iron are hard but brittle; nichrome is used as heating wire, not for hardness.

1.s: Which one of the following elements exist in liquid state at room temperature?
1.x: Bromine is the only non-metal liquid at room temperature (mercury is the liquid metal); H2, O2 are gases and iodine a solid.

1.s: Which of the following metals is most ductile in nature?
1.x: Gold is the most malleable and ductile metal (1 g can be drawn into ~2 km of wire); silver comes next.

1.s: Which of the following is an example of chemical change?
o: Dispersion of white light into the light of 7 colours when passed through a prism.
Wet soil lump, when dried, gets fragile.
1.x: Cooking softens vegetables through irreversible changes in their chemical composition – a chemical change. Dispersion, drying of soil and dissolving salt are physical changes.

1.s: Which one of the following noble gases is not found in the atmosphere?
1.x:
Official key / most books: radon is not found in the atmosphere. Strictly: radon is present in trace amounts, released from radium decay in rocks and soil (NCERT Chemistry XII ch.7).
Radon is the radioactive noble gas; books list it as not a constituent of the atmosphere, while argon, krypton and xenon are.

1.s:
Consider the following statements

I. The carat is a unit of purity for gold alloys.

II. 18 carat gold is 24 parts pure gold and 6 parts another metal.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
1.x: Carat measures gold purity (I true). 18 carat = 18 parts gold in 24 (75%), not '24 parts gold + 6 parts other metal', so II is false.

1.s: Heaviest metal of the following is made of
1.x: Uranium (density ~19 g/cm³) is far denser than silver (~10.5), copper (~9) and aluminium (~2.7).

1.s: Which is not a Lewis acid?
1.x: A Lewis acid accepts an electron pair. AlCl3, BF3 and FeCl3 are electron-deficient acceptors; NH3 donates its lone pair and is a Lewis base.

1.s:
Consider the following statements about mixture?

I. A substance can be separated into other kinds of matter by any physical process.

II. Dissolved sodium chloride can be separated from water by the physical process of evaporation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
1.x: I is wrong: only a mixture, not a pure substance, can be separated by physical means. II is right: evaporation leaves dissolved salt behind.

1.s: Which gas is known as ‘noble gas’?
1.x: Helium is a Group 18 noble (inert) gas with a full outer shell; hydrogen, oxygen and CO2 are not.

1.s: The number of valence electrons in the O2− ion is
1.x: Oxygen has 6 valence electrons; O2− gains 2 more, completing an octet of 8.

1.s: Which of the following is the electron configuration of a metallic element?
1.x: 2, 8, 8, 2 (calcium) has 2 valence electrons that are easily lost – a metal. 2, 8 and 2, 8, 8 are noble gases; 2, 8, 7 is chlorine.

1.s:
Which of the following causes the rusting of iron?

I. Oxidation

II. Reduction

III. Chemical reaction with oxygen

IV. Chemical reaction with CO2
1.x: Rusting is oxidation of iron by reaction with oxygen (and moisture): I and III. It is not reduction, and CO2 is not the cause.

1.s:
Which one of the following types of medicines is used for treating indigestion?

I. Antibiotic
II. Analgesic

III. Antacid
IV. Antiseptic
1.x: Antacids (milk of magnesia, baking soda) neutralise excess stomach acid and relieve indigestion; antibiotics, analgesics and antiseptics do not.

1.s: The pH value of water is
1.x: Pure water is neutral, pH 7 at 25 °C.

1.s: Aspirin is obtained from
1.x:
Official key / most books: obtained from a tree (willow bark). Strictly: modern aspirin is synthesised from salicylic acid made from phenol (Kolbe reaction), i.e. petrochemical feedstock (NCERT Chemistry XII ch.11).
Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) traces to salicin from willow-tree bark, so books key 'a tree'.

1.s: Which one of the following is used in the production of explosives?
1.x: Glycerol is nitrated to nitroglycerine, the explosive in dynamite.

1.s: The foul smell of dead fish is due to the compound
1.x: The smell of dead fish comes from amines, chiefly trimethylamine, formed by bacterial breakdown – amino compounds.

1.s: The most reactive among the halogen is
1.x: Halogen reactivity falls down the group; fluorine, the most electronegative element, is the most reactive.

1.s: What percentage of gold is there in 14 carat gold?
1.x: Pure gold is 24 carat, so 14 carat = 14/24 ≈ 58% gold (22 carat 91.6%, 18 carat 75%).

1.s: Which of the following are generally formed in combustion of saturated hydrocarbons?
