1.s: The astronaut in the ship sees the sky as:
1.x: With no atmosphere to scatter sunlight, the sky looks black to an astronaut even by day.

1.s: If the cover of a book looks red when seen through a piece of red glass, then the cover will look like
1.x: Red glass passes only red light: a red cover reflects red and looks red, a white cover also sends red through, so it could be red or white.

1.s: The flying of birds is a proof of Newton's
1.x: Wings push air down and back (action); air pushes the bird up and forward (reaction) – Newton's third law.

1.s: The image formed by astronomical telescope is
1.x: In an astronomical telescope (two convex lenses) the final image is virtual, inverted and highly magnified.

1.s:
Assertion (A) : Radio waves bend in a magnetic field.
Reason (R) : Radio waves are electromagnetic in nature.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
1.x: Radio waves are electromagnetic (R true) and, being uncharged, are not bent by a magnetic field (A false).

1.s: The SI unit of electrical resistivity of conductor is –
1.x: The SI unit of resistivity is the ohm-metre, so 'ohm' is the option that fits.

1.s: What is the unit of atmospheric pressure?
1.x: The bar (10⁵ Pa) is a common unit of atmospheric pressure (SI unit pascal); knot – speed, joule – energy, ohm – resistance.

1.s: Which one of the following statements is not true about cosmic rays?
o: They are made of highly energetic charged particles
1.x: Cosmic rays are streams of highly energetic charged particles (mostly protons), not electromagnetic waves.

1.s: What is the unit of measure of magnetic field?
1.x: The SI unit of magnetic field (flux density) is the tesla.

1.s: Bats can fly during dark nights and also prey. This is because :
o: The pupil of their eyes is large
Their night vision is very good
They produce ultrasonic waves and are guided by
1.x: Bats emit ultrasonic waves and navigate and hunt by their echoes (echolocation).

1.s: By which one of the following an old written material which cannot be read easily, can be read?
1.x: Infrared photography/reflectography brings out faded or obscured old writing, so IR rays.

1.s: Which of the following is attracted to the North pole of a permanent magnet?
o: North pole of another permanent magnet
A piece of iron that is not a permanent magnet
1.x: Unmagnetised iron is attracted by either pole; a north pole repels another north pole, and magnets do not attract static charges.

1.s: Which one of the following SI unit is not correctly matched?
1.x: The SI unit of pressure is the pascal; the dyne is the CGS unit of force, so 'Pressure – Dyne' is wrong.

1.s: Pressure inside a soap bubble is –
1.x: Surface tension makes the pressure inside a soap bubble higher than outside (excess pressure 4T/r).

1.s: The reverse effect of X-ray emission is
1.x: X-ray emission turns electron energy into photons; the photoelectric effect turns photon energy into ejected electrons – the reverse.

1.s:
Read the following statements–
Statement (A) : Ernest Rutherford said in Royal Society that a man will never be able to get nuclear energy.
Reason (R) : He was confident that the Law of Einstein will fail and the volume will not be converted to energy. Select your answer in the code given below :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (A) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(R) is correct but (A) is not correct
1.x: Rutherford did call atomic power 'moonshine' (British Association, 11 Sep 1933), so A is broadly true. R is false: he did not doubt Einstein's mass–energy law; he judged that splitting atoms consumed more energy than it released (official key: a).

1.s:
Consider the following statements :
Assertion (A) : Light coloured clothes are preferred in summer.
Reason (R) : Light colours are poor absorbers of heat. Select correct answer from the code given below :
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) correctly explains
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) does not correctly
1.x: Light colours reflect most heat and absorb little, so light clothes keep us cooler in summer – R explains A.

1.s: An object weighs the most
1.x: In vacuum there is no buoyant upthrust, so the object shows its full weight; air, hydrogen and water all reduce it.

1.s: A convex mirror is used to correct which of the following?
1.x: The stem means a convex lens: a converging (convex) lens corrects long sight (hypermetropia); myopia needs a concave lens.

1.s: The Equivalence Principle, also used in GPS time corrections, is the basis of which theory?
1.x: The equivalence principle underlies general relativity and is applied in GPS time corrections.
n: The Equivalence Principle is applied in General Relativity. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
The Equivalence Principle is used for GPS corrections. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
xa: **Doppler Principle** is applied in **radar speed guns** and **medical ultrasound**.
**Uncertainty Principle** is applied in **electron microscopes**.
**Pascal's Principle** is applied in **hydraulic lifts, brakes and presses**.

1.s: What is the older unit of electrical conductance, the reciprocal of resistance?
1.x: Conductance G = 1/R, and its older unit is the mho.
n: Conductance equals the reciprocal of resistance (G = 1/R). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
The older unit of conductance is mho. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]

1.s: What is the value of 1 horsepower in watts?
1.x: One horsepower equals 746 W. 3.6 × 10⁶ is joules in a kilowatt-hour, a trap figure.
1.tq: Recall 1 hp = 746 W.
n: One horsepower equals 746 watts. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
One kilowatt equals 1000 watts. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
One kilowatt-hour equals 3.6 × 10⁶ joules. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
xs: One horsepower = **746 watts**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Power** is measured in **watts (W)**; commercial units are **kilowatt (kW)** and **megawatt (MW)**.
xa: **One kilowatt** = **1000 watts**.
**1 V = 1 J/C** — one joule per coulomb.
**1 A = 1 C/s** — one coulomb per second.

1.s: What is the SI unit of conductivity?
1.x: Conductivity (1/ρ) is measured in S/m; siemens is the unit of conductance.
n: Resistivity is also measured in ohm-centimetres (Ω cm). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
The SI unit of conductivity is the siemens per metre (S/m). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
Conductivity is the reciprocal of resistivity (σ = 1/ρ). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
The SI unit of conductance is the siemens (S). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
xa: SI unit of **resistivity** is the **ohm-metre (Ω m)**.
**Conductance** = **1/R**; older unit **mho**.
⚠ **Conductivity** (S/m) is the reciprocal of **resistivity**; **conductance** (S) is the reciprocal of **resistance**.

1.s: What is the value of the elementary charge?
1.x: The elementary charge is 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C; one coulomb is the charge of 6.25 × 10¹⁸ electrons.
n: The SI unit of electric charge is the coulomb (C). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
Electric charge is also measured in esu and emu. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
The elementary charge is 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
One coulomb is the charge of 6.25 × 10¹⁸ electrons. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
xa: **Electric current** = **ampere**; **1 A = 1 C/s**.
**Potential difference** = **volt**; **1 V = 1 J/C**.
**Resistance** = **ohm**; **1 Ω = 1 V/A**.

1.s: Which principle explains the red shift of receding galaxies?
1.x: Red shift, blue shift and medical Doppler ultrasound all come from the Doppler principle.
n: The Doppler Principle explains red shift. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
The Doppler Principle explains blue shift. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
The Doppler Principle is used in medical ultrasound. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
The Doppler effect is applied to medical ultrasound. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
xa: **Equivalence Principle** → **General Relativity**, **GPS corrections**.
**Superposition Principle** → **interference**, **beats**, **standing waves**.
Ultrasound itself uses **high-frequency sound waves** and their **echoes**.

1.s: Which device converts sound vibrations into electrical signals by electromagnetic induction?
1.x: A dynamic microphone turns sound vibrations into electrical signals by electromagnetic induction.
n: Magnetic brakes use electromagnetic induction in trains. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
Dynamic microphones use electromagnetic induction. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
Induction motors use electromagnetic induction in industrial motors. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
Metal detectors use electromagnetic induction. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
xa: All of these are uses of **electromagnetic induction**.
**Generators** (power generation) and **transformers** (voltage conversion) also use it.
**Wireless charging** of **mobile phones** and **electric vehicles** works by induction.

1.s: What is the SI unit of resistivity?
1.x: Resistivity is measured in ohm-metre (Ω m), since ρ = RA/l. Ohm is for resistance and S/m is for conductivity.
1.tq: Discriminate resistance, resistivity and conductivity units.
n: The SI unit of resistivity is the ohm-metre (Ω m). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
The SI unit of potential difference or voltage is the volt (V). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
The SI unit of resistance is the ohm (Ω). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
The SI unit of conductivity is the siemens per metre (S/m). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
xs: The SI unit of resistivity is the **ohm-metre (Ω m)**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Ohm (Ω)** is the unit of **resistance**; **volt (V)** is the unit of **potential difference**.
**Siemens per metre (S/m)** is the unit of **conductivity**.
xa: Resistivity is also expressed in **ohm-centimetres (Ω cm)**.
**Conductivity** is the **reciprocal of resistivity** — **σ = 1/ρ**.
**Conductance** = **1/R**, unit **siemens (S)**, older unit **mho**.

1.s: Which principle explains wavefront propagation, reflection and refraction of waves?
1.x: Huygens' principle treats every point on a wavefront as a source, explaining propagation, reflection and refraction.
n: Huygens’ Principle explains wavefront propagation. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
Huygens’ Principle explains reflection of waves. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
Huygens’ Principle explains refraction of waves. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
xa: Huygens' Principle also explains **diffraction** and **interference** of **light**.
**Superposition Principle** explains **beats in sound** and **standing waves**.
**Uncertainty Principle** limits **precision** in **quantum measurements**.

1.s: Microwave ovens heat food primarily because microwaves of approximately which frequency cause water molecules to rotate?
1.x: Microwave ovens use microwaves of about 2.45 GHz, which make water molecules rotate and thereby generate heat.
1.tq: Separate MHz from GHz while retaining the exact numerical value.
xs: Microwave ovens use microwaves of about **2.45 GHz**, which make **water molecules rotate** → heat — option **(4)**.
Options (1)-(3) shift the unit or decimal; the notes give **2.45 GHz**.
xa: **Induction cooktop** = **electromagnetic induction** (eddy currents in an iron/steel vessel).
**Pressure cooker**: higher pressure **raises boiling point** to about **120 C**.
**Refrigerator** = **vapour-compression** cycle.

1.s: In a vapour-compression refrigerator, when does the refrigerant absorb heat?
1.x: The refrigerant absorbs heat while evaporating inside and releases it at the condenser.
xa: This is the **vapour-compression** cycle.
**Induction cooktops** use **electromagnetic induction**.
**RO purifier**: pressure applied **against osmosis** through a **semi-permeable membrane**.

1.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about household appliances?
o: An LED emits light by electroluminescence at a p-n junction
An RO purifier applies pressure in the direction of osmosis
A pressure cooker cooks faster because higher pressure raises the boiling point
In a pressure cooker water boils at about 120 C
1.x: An RO purifier applies pressure against osmosis to push water through the semi-permeable membrane.
xa: **Refrigerator** = vapour-compression cycle.
**Microwave oven** works at about **2.45 GHz**.
**Induction cooktop** heats by **eddy currents** in an iron/steel vessel.

1.s: On which principle does wireless charging work?
1.x: Wireless charging, like generators, transformers and induction cooktops, works by electromagnetic induction.
n: Generators are used for power generation through electromagnetic induction. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
Transformers are used for voltage conversion through electromagnetic induction. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
Induction cooktops use electromagnetic induction for heating. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
Wireless charging uses electromagnetic induction for mobile phones. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
Wireless charging uses electromagnetic induction for electric vehicles. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
xa: **Magnetic brakes** in **trains** use electromagnetic induction.
**Dynamic microphones** and **induction motors** also use it.
**EMI sensors** and **metal detectors** work on induction.

1.s: Which process is used for desalination of sea water and purification of water by removing ions and bacteria?
1.x: Reverse osmosis pushes water through a membrane against the osmotic gradient, leaving salts and bacteria behind, so it desalinates and purifies water.
1.tq: Discriminate osmosis from reverse osmosis.
n: Reverse osmosis is used for desalination of seawater. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 48-51]
Reverse osmosis is used for purification of water. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 48-51]
Reverse osmosis removes ions from water. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 48-51]
Reverse osmosis removes bacteria from water. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 48-51]
xs: **Reverse osmosis** desalinates seawater and purifies water, so option **(1)** is correct.
In reverse osmosis **external pressure** on the **concentrated side** moves solvent from **high to low** concentration.
It **removes ions and bacteria** and is used for **desalination of seawater**.
Plain **osmosis** moves water the other way — **low to high** solute concentration — so it cannot purify water.
xa: **Plant roots** absorb water by **osmosis**.
Osmosis occurs through a **semipermeable membrane**.
An **RO purifier** applies pressure **against osmosis** to push water through the membrane.

1.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about osmosis?
o: Plant roots absorb water by osmosis
Solvent moves from low to high solute concentration
In reverse osmosis, pressure is applied on the dilute side
1.x: In reverse osmosis external pressure is applied on the concentrated side.
n: The solvent in osmosis is water. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 48-51]
In osmosis, solvent moves from low solute concentration to high solute concentration. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 48-51]
Plant roots absorb water by osmosis. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 48-51]
Reverse osmosis applies external pressure on the concentrated side. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 48-51]
xa: In **reverse osmosis** solvent moves from **high to low** concentration.
Uses of reverse osmosis: **desalination** and **water purification** — removes **ions and bacteria**.
Osmosis needs a **semipermeable membrane**.

1.s: On which principle does an induction cooktop work?
1.x: An induction cooktop heats by electromagnetic induction and eddy currents; LEDs work on electroluminescence.
1.tq: one-liner

1.s: To about what temperature does a pressure cooker raise the boiling point of water?
1.x: Higher pressure raises the boiling point to about 120 C, so food cooks faster.
1.tq: one-liner

1.s: How is a fuse connected in a household circuit?
1.x: A fuse works on the heating effect, has a low melting point and is connected in series.
1.tq: one-liner

1.s: Which device produces the microwaves in a microwave oven?
1.x: A magnetron produces microwaves of about 2.45 GHz that make water molecules in food rotate and heat up.

1.s: What is the conventional direction of electric current?
o: Along the direction of electron flow
1.x: Conventional current flows positive to negative, opposite to electron flow.
n: Small currents are measured in milliamperes (mA) and microamperes (μA). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
The conventional direction of current is from positive to negative. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
The direction of electron flow is from negative to positive. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
xa: **1 A = 1 C/s** — one coulomb per second.
High resistances are measured in **kilohms (kΩ)** and **megohms (MΩ)**.
One coulomb = charge of **6.25 × 10¹⁸ electrons**.

1.s: On which principle does a hydraulic lift work?
1.x: A hydraulic lift follows Pascal's principle; buoyancy is Archimedes' and wing lift Bernoulli's.
n: Archimedes’ Principle explains buoyancy. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
Archimedes’ Principle explains floating and sinking. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
Bernoulli’s Principle explains lift on an aeroplane wing. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
Bernoulli’s Principle explains blood flow. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
Lift on an aeroplane is explained by Bernoulli’s Principle. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
xa: Archimedes' Principle is applied in **ships**, **hydrometers** and **submarines** (**ballast tanks**).
Bernoulli's Principle is applied in **atomisers**, **carburettors** and **Venturi tubes**.
Pascal's Principle also works in **syringes** and **hydraulic brakes**.

1.s: Where should the object be placed for a convex lens to act as a magnifying glass?
1.x: Within F a convex lens forms a virtual, erect, magnified image, as in a magnifying glass.
n: A convex lens forms a virtual, erect, magnified image when the object is within F. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 64-76]
A convex lens is used as a magnifying glass. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 64-76]
A magnifying glass produces a virtual magnified image when the object is within F. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 64-76]
xa: A convex lens in a **camera** forms a **real inverted image** on **film or a sensor**.
A **projector** forms a **magnified real image** on a **screen**.
The **eye lens** forms a **real image** on the **retina**.

1.s: A camera, a compound microscope and a telescope all use which of the following to form real images?
1.x: A camera, a compound microscope and a telescope all use convex lenses to form real images.
n: A convex lens is used in a camera. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 64-76]
A convex lens is used in a microscope. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 64-76]
A convex lens is used in a telescope. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 64-76]
xa: **Combinations** of lenses are used in **microscopes**, **telescopes** and **binoculars** to **correct aberrations**.
⚠ Some **Galileo telescopes** use a **concave** lens as the **eyepiece**.
A **projector** uses a convex lens for a **magnified real image** on a screen.

1.s: Which of the following statements about myopia is incorrect?
o: It is corrected using a concave lens.
The image of a distant object forms in front of the retina.
The corrective lens has positive power.
1.x: Option D is incorrect: myopia is corrected with a concave lens of negative power, not positive. The image forms in front of the retina.
1.tq: Recall the lens and power sign for each defect.
n: Myopia is short-sightedness. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 64-76]
Myopia forms the image in front of the retina. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 64-76]
Myopia is corrected with a concave diverging lens. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 64-76]
A myopia-correcting lens has negative power, such as –2 D. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 64-76]
A concave lens is used in spectacles for myopia. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 64-76]
A concave lens has negative power. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 64-76]
xs: The incorrect statement is "**the corrective lens has positive power**", so option **(4)** is the answer.
Myopia is corrected by **spectacles with a concave lens**, which **diverges rays** so the image forms on the **retina**.
A **concave** lens has **negative** power; only a **convex** lens has **positive** power.
xa: Power of a lens = **reciprocal of focal length** in **metres**; unit **dioptre (D)**.
Concave lenses are also used in **peephole / door viewers** for a **wide field of view**.
Some **Galileo telescopes** use a concave lens as the **eyepiece**.

1.s: An ice-skater spins faster on pulling in the arms because of the conservation of which quantity?
1.x: Conservation of angular momentum explains the skater's spin and planetary orbits.
n: The Conservation of Angular Momentum explains ice-skater spin. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
The Conservation of Angular Momentum explains planetary orbits. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
xa: ⚠ **Conservation of (linear) Momentum** explains **recoil of a gun** and **rocket propulsion**.
**Conservation of Energy** applies to **roller coasters** and **pendulums**.
**Archimedes' Principle** explains **buoyancy** and the **floating of ships**.

1.s: Which of the following is associated with Conservation of Momentum?
o: Recoil of a gun and rocket propulsion
1.x: Gun recoil and rocket propulsion conserve momentum: the forward momentum of bullet or exhaust equals the backward momentum of the gun or rocket.
1.tq: Recall the applications of momentum conservation.
n: The Conservation of Momentum explains recoil of a gun. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
The Conservation of Momentum explains rocket propulsion. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
The Conservation of Momentum explains recoil of a gun. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
The Conservation of Momentum explains rocket launch. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
xs: Conservation of Momentum explains the **recoil of a gun and rocket propulsion**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Hydraulic lift and syringe** follow **Pascal's Principle**, not momentum conservation.
xa: **Conservation of Angular Momentum** explains **ice-skater spin** and **planetary orbits**.
**Conservation of Energy** applies to **roller coasters**, **pendulums** and **power generation**.
**Bernoulli's Principle** explains **lift on an aeroplane wing**.

1.s: What is the optical action of a burning glass on sun rays?
1.x: A burning glass is a convex lens that converges sun rays to a point and can ignite paper.
1.tq: Recall that a convex lens converges light.
n: A burning glass converges sun rays. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 64-76]
xs: A burning glass **converges** sun rays, so option **(3)** is correct.
A **burning glass** is a **convex** lens — it **converges sun rays**.
xa: A convex lens is also a **magnifying glass** — a **virtual magnified image** with the object within F.
A **concave** lens **diverges** rays — used in spectacles for **myopia**.
A convex lens has **positive** power.

1.s: Which instrument is used to test the purity of milk?
1.x: A lactometer checks the purity of milk by measuring its specific gravity.

1.s: What does a hygrometer measure?
1.x: A hygrometer measures humidity; an anemometer measures wind speed and a barometer measures pressure.

1.s: Which property of a body is measured by its mass?
1.x: Mass is the measure of inertia, the tendency of a body to resist a change in its motion.

1.s: If the momentum of a body is doubled, by how much does its kinetic energy increase?
1.x: KE = p squared / 2m, so doubling momentum makes KE four times, an increase of 300%.

1.s: Which state of matter is called the fourth state of matter?
1.x: Plasma (ionised gas) is the fourth state; Bose-Einstein condensate is the fifth.

1.s: Who called hydrogen 'inflammable air' in 1766?
1.x: Henry Cavendish identified hydrogen in 1766 and called it 'inflammable air'.

1.s: Which is the second most abundant element in the Earth's crust after oxygen?
1.x: Silicon is the second most abundant element in the crust, after oxygen.

1.s: On which type of current does a transformer work?
1.x: A transformer works only on AC, because it needs a changing magnetic field.

1.s: Why is a bird sitting on a single live wire safe?
o: Its body has very high resistance
There is no potential difference across its body
The current in the wire is AC
1.x: Both feet are on the same wire at the same potential, so no current flows through the bird.

1.s: What does a light year measure?
1.x: A light year is the distance light travels in one year; it is a unit of distance.

1.s: Decibel is the unit of what?
1.x: Decibel measures sound level (loudness); pascal is the unit of pressure.

1.s: Which clock gives the most exact time?
1.x: An atomic (caesium) clock keeps the most exact time.

1.s: A fan running under a lamp on AC supply sometimes seems to turn backwards. What is this effect called?
1.x: The lamp flickers with the AC supply; if the flicker matches the blade speed, the fan seems to stop or reverse. This is the stroboscopic effect.

1.s: In terms of electrons, what is oxidation?
1.x: OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain of electrons.

1.s: Which element is always present in alkaloids?
1.x: Alkaloids are plant compounds that contain nitrogen.

1.s: An unmagnetised iron bar is brought near a bar magnet. Which pole of the magnet attracts it?
1.x: Unmagnetised iron is attracted by either pole; only repulsion proves that a bar is a magnet.

1.s: About what percentage of inhaled air is oxygen?
1.x: Inhaled air has about 21% oxygen and 78% nitrogen; exhaled air has about 16% oxygen.

1.s: Which one of the following is not considered as a macronutrient?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
1.x: Macronutrients are needed in large amounts and give energy or bulk: carbohydrates, proteins and fats. Minerals (and vitamins) are needed in small amounts and are classed as micronutrients.

1.s: What is the scientific name of Ashwagandha?
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Ashwagandha is Withania somnifera (family Solanaceae). Withania coagulans is the 'paneer dodi' (Indian cheese-maker) and Solanum nigrum is black nightshade.

1.s:
A statement is given followed by two conclusions.
Select the correct response from the given options.
Statement: Aschelminthes are called roundworms.
Conclusion:
i. The body of the aschelminthes is circular in cross-section.
ii. Roundworms have organ-system level of body organisation.
1.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
1.x:
Printed key: only (i) follows from the statement. Strictly, both (i) and (ii) are true facts (PMF General Science p.89 / NCERT XI: organ-system level), so a fact-check reading gives 'both'.
The name 'roundworm' comes from the body being circular in cross-section, so conclusion (i) follows from the statement. Conclusion (ii) is a true fact (Aschelminthes have organ-system level of organisation) but does not follow from the statement about the name.

1.s: A flower is brightly coloured, scented and secretes nectar. It is most probably pollinated by
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x: Bright colour, scent and nectar are adaptations that attract insects, so such a flower is insect-pollinated (entomophily). Wind- and water-pollinated flowers are small, dull and without nectar or scent.

1.s: Goiter is characterized by:
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
1.x: Goitre is the enlargement of the thyroid gland, mostly due to iodine deficiency.

1.s: Which of the following is pseudocereal
1.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
1.x: Buckwheat (kuttu) is a pseudocereal: its seeds are used like grain but it is not a grass (family Polygonaceae). Amaranth and quinoa are other pseudocereals.

1.s: According to Kohlberg, which is the highest stage of moral reasoning?
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
1.x: Kohlberg's sixth and highest stage is the 'universal ethical principle' orientation (post-conventional). Law and order is stage 4, social contract stage 5 and punishment-avoidance stage 1.

1.s:
Consider the following actions :
1. Detection of car crash/collision which results in the deployment of airbags almost instantaneously
2. Detection of accidental free fall of a laptop towards the ground which results in the immediate turning off of the hard drive
3. Detection of the tilt of the smart-phone which results in the rotation of display between portrait and landscape mode In how many of the above actions is the function of accelerometer required?
1.x: All three use accelerometers: airbag crash detection, laptop free-fall detection and phone screen rotation by tilt.

1.s:
In which of the following are hydrogels used?
1. Controlled drug delivery in patients.
2. Mobile air-conditioning systems.
3. Preparation of industrial lubricants.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
1.x: Hydrogels are well established in controlled drug delivery, contact lenses and wound dressings. Mobile air-conditioning and industrial lubricants are not standard uses. UPSC official key (Set A Q.36): (a) 1 only.

1.s:
In which of the following are hydrogels used ?
1. Controlled drug delivery in patients
2. Mobile air-conditioning systems
3. Preparation of industrial lubricants
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
1.x: Hydrogels are well established in controlled drug delivery, contact lenses and wound dressings. Mobile air-conditioning and industrial lubricants are not standard uses. UPSC official key (Set A Q.36): (a) 1 only.

1.s:
Consider the following features of newer models of motor cars.

I. Radial tyres

II. Streamlined body

III. Multipoint fuel injection

IV. Catalytic converter with exhaust
Which of these features make the new models of motor cars more fuel efficient?
1.x:
Official key / most books: II and III. Strictly: radial tyres (I) also cut rolling resistance, so I, II and III improve efficiency (no such option).
A streamlined body (less drag) and multipoint fuel injection (better combustion) raise fuel efficiency. A catalytic converter only cuts emissions. Radial tyres also help through lower rolling resistance, but the standard key is II and III.

1.s: Where is the Black Box fitted in planes?
1.x: The black box (flight data and cockpit voice recorders) is fitted in the tail section, the part most likely to survive a crash.

1.s: From environmental considerations, which of the following is a better option to serve Tea or trains?
o: Serving in glass cups or metal glasses, which are reusable
1.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
1.x: Reusable glass or metal cups create no waste. Paper cups are plastic-lined, plastic glasses are single-use, and kulhads, though biodegradable, use topsoil and kiln fuel each time.

1.s: Which part of the flower becomes the fruit?
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: After fertilisation the ovary develops into the fruit and the ovules into seeds.

1.s: Viscosity is measured in:
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
1.x: Viscosity is measured in poise (CGS unit); the SI unit is the pascal-second (1 Pa·s = 10 poise).

1.s:
Match the following columns I and II and choose the CORRECT answer from the given options.
Column I (Phylum):

A. Ctenophora

B. Porifera

C. Coelenterata (Cnidaria)

D. Echinodermata
Column II (Distinctive features):

1. Choanocytes

2. Bioluminescence

3. Water vascular system

4. Polyp and Medusa
1.src: APPSC Deputy Educational Officer Screening Test (General Stu
1.x: Ctenophores show bioluminescence, sponges (Porifera) have choanocytes, Cnidaria have polyp and medusa forms, and echinoderms have a water vascular system: A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3. (Biology, filed under polity by mistake.)

1.s:
Consider the following two statements and select the correct option.
Statement I: In a given medium, the speed of sound remains constant regardless of temperature changes.
Statement II: Sound waves are longitudinal waves, meaning the particles of the medium vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation.
o: Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
Both Statement I and statement II are true.
Both Statement I and statement II are false.
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
1.x: Statement I is false – the speed of sound in a medium rises with temperature (about 0.6 m/s per °C in air). Statement II is true: sound waves are longitudinal.

1.s:
Consider the following two statements and select the correct option.
Statement I: The Haber process is an industrial method used to produce ammonia by reacting nitrogen and hydrogen gases under high temperature and pressure in the presence of an iron catalyst.
Statement II: The Contact process is an important industrial method used to manufacture sulphuric acid, which involves the catalytic oxidation of sulphur dioxide to sulphur trioxide using vanadium pentoxide (V2O5) as a catalyst.
o: Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
Both statement I and statement II are true.
Both statement I and statement II are false.
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
1.x: Both are true: the Haber process makes ammonia from N2 and H2 over an iron catalyst, and the Contact process makes sulphuric acid by oxidising SO2 to SO3 over V2O5.

1.s:
Consider the following two statements and select the correct option.
Statement I: The axial skeleton consists of the skull, vertebral column, rib cage and sternum, providing structural support and protection to vital organs.
Statement II: The tibia is the longest and strongest bone in the human body, located in the upper arm.
o: Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
Both statement I and statement II are false.
Both statement I and statement II are true.
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
1.x: Statement I is true (skull, vertebral column, ribs and sternum form the axial skeleton). Statement II is false: the femur (thigh) is the longest and strongest bone, and the tibia is in the lower leg, not the arm.

1.s: Sun drying is a method of:
1.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
1.x: Sun drying removes moisture so that microbes cannot grow; it is a traditional method of food preservation (dehydration).

1.s: In periodic table helium is placed at
1.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
1.x: Helium is a noble gas in Group 18, period 1, so it sits at the top right corner of the periodic table.

1.s: Planets revolve around the sun due to gravitational force. Similarly, electrons revolve around the nucleus due to ____.
1.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
1.x: Electrons are held in orbit round the positive nucleus by electrostatic (Coulomb) attraction, just as gravity keeps planets round the Sun.

1.s: Which of the following has the same atomic number and atomic weight?
1.x: Ordinary hydrogen (protium) has one proton and no neutron, so its atomic number and mass number are both 1; helium is 2 and 4.

1.s: Inflammable air is:
1.x: Henry Cavendish (1766) called hydrogen 'inflammable air' because it burns; the name 'hydrogen' was given later by Lavoisier.

1.s: Yellow and Orange fruits belong to the group of
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
1.x: Yellow and orange fruits are rich in vitamins (carotene/vitamin A, vitamin C) and minerals, so they are protective (regulatory) foods.

1.s: In Pavlovian conditioning paradigm as developed originally which of the following was used as independent variable?
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
1.x: In Pavlov's original paradigm the experimenter varied the number of pairings of the conditioned stimulus (bell) with the unconditioned stimulus (food) – the independent variable; response magnitude and latency were the measured (dependent) variables.

1.s: Which of the following colours would have largest wavelength?
1.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
1.x: In the visible spectrum (VIBGYOR) wavelength rises from violet to red; of orange, yellow, indigo and violet, orange has the longest wavelength.

1.s: Which of the following is a noble gas?
1.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
1.x: Helium is a noble (inert) gas of Group 18; hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen are reactive.

1.s: It would be less safe to fill a gas balloon with the following gas:
1.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
1.x: Hydrogen is lighter than air but highly inflammable, so it is the least safe gas for a balloon; helium is inert and safe.

1.s: 'Volume of a given mass of a gas is inversely proportional to its pressure at a constant temperature'. This statement is associated with:
1.src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer (Mains) General Studies &
1.x: Boyle's Law: at constant temperature the volume of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to its pressure. Charles's Law relates volume and temperature.

1.s: A sensitive magnetic field instrument can be effectively shielded from the external magnetic field by placing it inside which of the following materials?
1.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
1.x: Soft iron of high permeability draws the magnetic field lines into itself and so shields the space inside it (magnetic shielding); plastic, wood or a good conductor do not stop a steady magnetic field.

1.s: Ignoring friction of air, if one brick and one feather are released to ground from top of a building, which one reaches ground first?
1.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
1.x: Without air resistance all bodies fall with the same acceleration g whatever their mass, so the brick and the feather reach the ground together (Galileo; shown on the Moon by Apollo 15).

1.s: Which liquid would boil last?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
1.x: Mercury boils at about 357°C, far above water (100°C), benzene (80°C) and ethyl alcohol (78°C), so it boils last.

1.s: Which of the following is NOT an example of friction?
o: Applying brakes to stop a moving car
Revolution of the planets around the sun
1.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
1.x: Planets revolve round the Sun because of gravity in near-vacuum space, so there is no friction; brakes, striking a match and walking all depend on friction.

1.s: A Ball thrown outside from an artificial satellite revolving around the Earth will –
o: Revolve around the Earth in the same orbit with the
1.x: A ball released from an orbiting satellite already has the satellite's orbital speed, so it keeps falling round the Earth in the same orbit, like the satellite itself.

1.s: The test in which the scorer is asked to rank samples in a decreasing or increasing order of same characteristics is:
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
1.x: In a ranking test (sensory evaluation) the judge arranges samples in increasing or decreasing order of one characteristic, such as sweetness.

1.s:
Match
List-I with
List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List-1 (Physicists):
A. WK Roentgen
B. Victor Francis Hess
C. Ernest Orlando Lawrence
D. CH Townes
List-2 (Major contribution/discovery):
1. Cosmic radiation
2. Maser
3. X-rays
4. Cyclotron
1.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
1.x: Roentgen discovered X-rays, Hess cosmic radiation, Lawrence invented the cyclotron and Townes the maser, so A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2. Off-topic science, moved.

1.s: If egg shell is carefully dissolved in acid and then immersed in salt water, then the shell?
1.src: APPSC AE (Environmental) Mains General Studies & Mental Abil
1.x: Acid dissolves the calcium carbonate shell, leaving the semi-permeable membrane; in strong salt water (hypertonic) water leaves the egg by osmosis, so it shrinks. Off-topic science, moved.

1.s: Rectifiers convert ____.
1.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
1.x: A rectifier converts alternating current (AC) into direct current (DC). (Moved to science in daily life.)

1.s: Saponification is the reaction between
o: A fat and a strong acid
A fat and a strong base
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Saponification is the hydrolysis of a fat (or oil) with a strong base such as NaOH, giving soap and glycerol. An acid-base reaction is neutralisation.

1.s: Saurology is the
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Saurology (herpetology of lizards) is the study of lizards.

1.s: Who among of the following is not an exponent of Humanistic Realism?
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
1.x: Humanistic realism is a 16th-century Renaissance school whose exponents were Erasmus, Rabelais and Milton; Aristotle is an ancient Greek philosopher, not one of its exponents. Off-subject (philosophy of education).

1.s: Who opined, "The world is continuously evolving towards greater degree of perfection that is God." It is the opinion of
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
1.x: The idea that the world is continuously evolving towards a greater perfection that is God (the Divine) is Sri Aurobindo's theory of spiritual evolution. Aristotle (the printed key) spoke of an unmoved mover, not of the world evolving into God; Plato and Russell do not hold this view. Off-subject (philosophy of education).

1.s: New ideas (Eureka) suddenly come in the minds of the creative children in which of the following stage?
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
1.x: In Wallas's stages of creativity (preparation, incubation, illumination, verification) the sudden 'Eureka' insight comes at illumination. Off-subject (educational psychology).

1.s: Which of the following forces is responsible for all the nucleons to be concentrated in the nucleus?
1.src: APPSC Deputy Inspector of Survey, Technical Assistant in AP
1.x: The strong nuclear force, short-range and far stronger than electrostatic repulsion, binds protons and neutrons in the nucleus. Off-subject (physics).

1.s: The most malleable metal is
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x: Gold is the most malleable (and ductile) metal; it can be beaten into leaves a few atoms thick. Silver is next; aluminium and iron are far less malleable.

1.s: The magnitude of root pressure would be minimum during
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
1.x: Root pressure is lowest in summer, when heavy transpiration pulls water up and the positive root pressure largely disappears. It is highest in the rainy season, when absorption is high and transpiration low, so Rainy season was wrong.

1.s: A metric chain of 20 metre length consists of ____ links.
1.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
1.x: A 20 m metric chain has 100 links of 0.2 m (20 cm) each.

1.s: The permissible percentage overload on DG sets for 1 hour in every 12 hours of operation is
1.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
1.x: Prime-rated diesel generator sets are allowed a 10% overload for 1 hour in every 12 hours of operation. Off-topic (electrical engineering).

1.s: Temperature and time used to sterilise glassware in hot air oven
1.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
1.x: A hot air oven sterilises glassware at 160°C with a holding time of one hour (170°C for 30 min, 180°C for 20 min); shorter times at 160°C are not enough. Off-topic (microbiology).

1.s: Sum of exterior angles of a convex polygon is
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: The exterior angles of any convex polygon, one at each vertex, always add up to 360°. Off-topic (mathematics).

1.s: What happens if you plug in a heater device rated for 110 V, 50 Hz in a household AC electric supply plug in India?
o: It burns out within minutes or even in seconds
Its heat supply would be poorer than its rated value.
You cannot use such a device in an Indian Plug
1.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
1.x: On India's 230 V supply a 110 V heater draws about (230/110)² ≈ 4 times its rated power, so its element burns out quickly. Off-topic (physics).

1.s: Humans have ____ of chromosomes, or tightly wrapped strands of DNA, that provide the instructions for metabolic processes, building cellular and tissue components, as well as other body functions.
1.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
1.x: Humans have 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs (22 pairs of autosomes + 1 pair of sex chromosomes). Off-topic (biology).

1.s: In which of the following season human beings require food with more fat content
1.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
1.x: In winter the body needs more energy to keep warm, so fat-rich (energy-dense) food is needed most then. Off-topic (nutrition).

1.s: The Right Hemisphere of the brain handles?
1.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
1.x: The right cerebral hemisphere is dominant for spatial abilities (also face recognition, visual imagery); language is mainly left-hemisphere. Off-topic (psychology).

1.s: In which season Vitamin A is required in higher quantities?
1.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
1.x: No standard source (ICMR-NIN RDA) gives a season-specific vitamin A requirement; deficiency signs such as night blindness peak in the hot pre-harvest season, while the printed key says winter. Left unkeyed. Off-topic (nutrition).

1.s: Carbohydrates are organic compounds with the basic structure:
1.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
1.x: Carbohydrates have the general formula Cx(H2O)y – carbon with hydrogen and oxygen in the 2:1 ratio of water (e.g. glucose C6H12O6). A science question, moved to book 5.

1.s: Which of the following is a diuretic
1.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Furosemide (loop diuretic), mannitol (osmotic diuretic) and acetazolamide (carbonic anhydrase inhibitor) all increase urine output, so all of these are diuretics.

1.s: The outer shell of the egg is composed of
1.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
1.x: An egg shell is about 95% calcium carbonate (CaCO3). Off-topic (general science), moved.

1.s: Which is the most abundant element by mass in human body?
1.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
1.x: Oxygen is the most abundant element by mass in the human body (~65%), followed by carbon and hydrogen. Off-topic (general science), moved.

1.s: When an iron nail gets rusted, its weight?
o: Increase or decrease depends on temperature and pressure
1.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
1.x: Rust is hydrated iron oxide; the iron combines with oxygen and water, so the weight increases. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: Which metal has the maximum use as pure metal?
1.x: Aluminium is keyed: light, abundant and corrosion-resistant, it is used very widely in nearly pure form (foils, cans, sheets, conductors); silver is scarce and iron is used mostly as steel. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: Which of the following is an inorganic lubricant?
1.src: APPSC 2018 Special Qualifying Test for Appointment by Promot
1.x: Graphite is an inorganic layered form of carbon used as a solid lubricant; lanolin, mineral oil and PTFE are organic. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: A soap molecule has two ends, one of which is an ionic end and the other is a carbonic chain end. Which part of the soap molecule interacts with oily dirt to enable cleansing?
o: The end that is closer to the oil molecule
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: The hydrocarbon (carbon-chain) tail dissolves in oil and grips the dirt, while the ionic end faces water, forming micelles. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: Which of the following features is NOT common in Chordates and non-chordates?
1.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
1.x: Printed key: bilateral symmetry – all chordates are bilaterally symmetrical, but many non-chordates (cnidarians, adult echinoderms) are radial, so it is not common to both groups. Off-topic (zoology), moved.

1.s: If a piece of wood and a piece of iron are placed in a fridge and taken out after 15 minutes, which one would feel more cold on touching?
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
1.x: Iron is a good conductor of heat, so it draws heat from the hand faster and feels colder, though both are at the same temperature. Wood is a poor conductor.

1.s: Commonly used absorbable suture material is
1.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Catgut, made from animal intestine (collagen), is the classic absorbable suture. Silk and nylon are non-absorbable, and fascia lata is a tissue graft.

1.s: Skull of mammals is
1.src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022
1.x: Mammals (and amphibians) have a dicondylic skull, joined to the vertebral column by two occipital condyles. Reptiles and birds have a monocondylic skull.

1.s:
Consider the following statements in respect of 'pi' (π)

a. Pi is the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter.

b. Pi is a rational number
Which of the above statement/s is/are correct?
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
1.x: Only a is correct: pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, and it is irrational (Aryabhata's 3.1416 is only an approximation), so statement b is false.

1.s: Why alum is used in the process of purifying drinking water?
1.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
1.x: Alum (potash alum) supplies Al3+ ions that neutralise the charge on suspended clay particles so they coagulate and settle. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: What is a change of position?
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x:
Most keys: Motion. Strictly: the change in position (a vector) is displacement (NCERT Class 9 ch. 8).
In school physics, motion is the change of position of a body with time, which is the key the paper gives. Strictly, the size and direction of the change in position is displacement, and distance is the path length.

1.s: "An object at rest will remain at rest and an object moving at a constant velocity will continue moving at a constant velocity, unless it is acted on by an unbalanced force". This law is called as ____.
1.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
1.x: Newton's first law (law of inertia): a body stays at rest or in uniform motion unless an unbalanced force acts on it. The second law gives F = ma, the third deals with action and reaction, and there is no fourth law.

1.s: Under what conditions the resistivity of the material does not change?
o: When the shape of the resistor is changed
When both the material and temperature are changed
1.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
1.x: Resistivity is a property of the material and its temperature, so it does not change when only the shape (length or area) of the resistor changes; resistance would change, resistivity would not.

1.s: Which of the following waves are used for common TV remote control?
1.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
1.x: Common TV remote controls use infrared (IR) light-emitting diodes. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: Which type of sound waves can propagate in solids?
1.x: Solids can carry both longitudinal and transverse mechanical waves (like seismic P- and S-waves); fluids carry only longitudinal waves. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: A louder sound is produced by a wave that has a greater
1.src: AP High Court Common Test for Multiple Posts 2026
1.x: Loudness depends on amplitude – a larger amplitude gives a louder sound; frequency decides pitch. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s:
Identify the correct pair(s) from the given pairs with respect to minerals and their function and choose the correct option.

I. Zinc - For insulin production

II. Phosphorus - Development of strong bones and teeth

III. Fluoride - Makes enamel of teeth hard and prevents dental caries
1.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers, Polytechnic Lecturers Paper-I Genera
1.x: Zinc is needed for insulin synthesis and storage, phosphorus (with calcium) builds bones and teeth, and fluoride hardens tooth enamel and prevents caries – all three pairs are correct. Off-topic (nutrition), moved.

1.s:
Living systems are made up of various complex biomolecules which include carbohydrates. Match the following Group of Carbohydrates with their examples.
Group of Carbohydrates:
I. Monosaccharides
II. Oligosaccharides
III. Polysaccharides
Examples:
a. Cellulose
b. Ribose
c. Maltose
1.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
1.x: Ribose – monosaccharide, maltose – oligosaccharide (disaccharide), cellulose – polysaccharide. Off-topic (biology), moved.

1.s:
Which of the following are correct with reference to proteins?
i. They are made up of nucleotides.
ii. They are linear chains of amino acids.
iii. They are heteropolymer.
iv. They are homopolymer.
1.src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
1.x: Proteins are linear chains of amino acids and are heteropolymers (20 kinds of amino acids); nucleotides make nucleic acids. Off-topic (biology), moved.

1.s:
Match the phylum in column A with their features in column B.
Column A (Phylum):

I. Porifera

II. Cnidaria

III. Arthropoda
Column B (Features):

a. Presence of Ostia and Osculum

b. Available in two forms- Polyp and Medusa

c. Have jointed appendages.
1.x: Porifera – ostia and osculum, Cnidaria – polyp and medusa forms, Arthropoda – jointed appendages. Off-topic, moved.

1.s:
When it comes to the digestive system, which statements are true?

I. The pancreas produces digestive enzymes and insulin.

II. The small intestine is where most nutrient absorption occurs.

III. The gallbladder stores bile produced by the liver.
1.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon, Group-IV and Other Posts Gene
1.x: The pancreas makes digestive enzymes and insulin, most absorption is in the small intestine, and the gall bladder stores bile – all three true. Off-topic, moved.

1.x: Micheli – mycology, Cuvier – palaeontology, Virchow – pathology, Stephen Hales – plant physiology. Off-topic, moved.

1.s:
Match the types of following of asexual reproduction in Column A with correct example in Column
B.
Column A:
A. Binary fission B. Budding
C. Regeneration
D. Spore formation
Column B: i. Amoeba ii. Yeast iii. Rhizopus iv. Planaria
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Binary fission – Amoeba, budding – yeast, regeneration – Planaria, spore formation – Rhizopus. Off-topic, moved.

1.s:
Which of the following is a correct match of organisms and patterns of organisation of cells in it?
Organism:

I. Sponges

II. Coelenterates

III. Platyhelminthes
Pattern of organisation of cells:

a. Tissue level of organisation

b. Cellular level of organisation

c. Organ level of organisation
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer (FRO) Paper-I General Studies & M
1.x: Sponges – cellular level, coelenterates – tissue level, Platyhelminthes – organ level. Off-topic, moved.

1.s:
Match the following using suitable codes:
A (Plant):
a. Fennel
b. Ginger
c. Garlic
d. Touch me not
B (Botanical Name):
I. Mimosa pudica
II. Foeniculum Vulgare
III. Zingiber officinale
IV. Allium Sativum
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x: Fennel – Foeniculum vulgare, ginger – Zingiber officinale, garlic – Allium sativum, touch-me-not – Mimosa pudica. Off-topic, moved.

1.s:
Match the following using suitable codes:
A (Medicinal Plant):
a. Sarpgandha
b. Isabgol
c. Arjuna
d. Sandal
B (Uses):
I. diuretic, refrigerant
II. nervous disorder
III. chronic constipation
IV. heart remedy
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x: Sarpagandha – nervous disorders (hypertension), isabgol – chronic constipation, arjuna – heart remedy, sandal – diuretic, refrigerant. Off-topic, moved.

1.s:
Match
List I (Physical quantities) with
List II (Units) and choose the correct option:
List I:
I. Electric current
II. Temperature
III. Luminous Intensity
List II:
a. candela
b. ampere
c. kelvin
1.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers, Polytechnic Lecturers Paper-I Genera
1.x: SI units: current – ampere, temperature – kelvin, luminous intensity – candela. Off-topic, moved.

1.src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I (Mains) General Studies & Mental Abil
1.x: Stomata – tiny pores on leaves, guard cells – open and close them, chloroplasts – contain chlorophyll, enzymes – biocatalysts. Off-topic, moved.

1.s: What is the resting rate heart for a normal person?
1.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
1.x: A normal adult resting heart rate is 60 to 100 beats per minute (American Heart Association); about 72 is the textbook average.

1.s: If Kilo is Thousand, then Deka is
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
1.x: Deka (deca) is the SI prefix for ten (10^1); kilo = 10^3, hecto = 10^2.

1.s:
Which of the following statements is correct with reference to sporopollenin?
i. The exine of pollen grains is made up of sporopollenin so that pollen grains can be preserved as fossils.
ii. It cannot withstand high temperatures.
iii. It is one of the most resistant organic materials.
iv. Enzymes can degrade it.
1.src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
1.x: Sporopollenin forms the exine; it is one of the most resistant organic materials, withstands high temperatures and strong acids and alkalis, and no enzyme is known to degrade it – so only i and iii. Moved.

1.s:
Match the given component of living tissues with the percentage of the total cellular mass.
Component:
I. Lipids
II. Proteins
III. Carbohydrates
IV. Nucleic acids
Percentage of the total cellular mass:
a. 5-7%
b. 10-15%
c. 3%
d. 2%
1.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
1.x: In a cell, proteins are 10–15%, nucleic acids 5–7%, carbohydrates 3% and lipids 2% of the mass (water 70–90%). Moved.

1.s: Which of the following is incorrect about the ultrasonic waves?
o: These waves are can be used for imaging
It cannot be heard by normal human ears
The speed of ultrasonic waves is more in denser media
The ultrasonic waves can travel through vacuum
1.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
1.x: Ultrasonic waves are mechanical sound waves and cannot travel through vacuum; they are inaudible, used for imaging and travel faster in denser media. Moved.

1.s:
Match the following from table A to Table B - Use of Salts
Table A:
I. Sodium Carbonate
II. Sodium Benzoate
III. Calcium Carbonate
IV. Calcium Phosphate
Table B:
1. Extraction of Metals
2. As Washing Soda, Manufacturing of Glass
3. As a Fertilizers
4. As a Food preservative for Pickles
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Sodium carbonate is washing soda used in glass-making, sodium benzoate is a food preservative, calcium carbonate is a flux in metal extraction and calcium phosphate is a fertiliser. Moved.

1.s:
Match the following From Table A to Table B - Uses of Acids as Food
Table A:
I. Butyric Acid
II. Maleic Acid
III. Stearic Acid
IV. Oxalic Acid
Table B:
1. Fats
2. Wood Sorrel
3. Apples
4. Rancid Butter
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Butyric acid is in rancid butter, malic acid ('Maleic' in the stem) in apples, stearic acid in fats and oxalic acid in wood sorrel. Moved.

1.s: The caramelization reactions require intense heat about
1.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers, Polytechnic Lecturers Paper-I Genera
1.x: Caramelisation of sucrose needs about 170 °C (it begins near 160 °C); 100 °C only boils water and 200-240 °C burns the sugar.

1.s: Out of the below, what is the example of a chemical reaction?
1.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
1.x: Rusting forms a new substance (iron oxide), so it is a chemical change; freezing, glowing of a lamp filament and dissolving salt are physical changes. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: Oxidation process means
1.src: APPSC Group-II Paper-I General Studies & Mental Ability 2019
1.x: In chemistry oxidation is the loss of electrons (reduction = gain of electrons). Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: Which of these is the change of gaseous state directly to solid state without going through liquid state?
1.src: APPSC Deputy Educational Officer Screening Test (General Stu
1.x: The change of a gas directly into a solid is deposition (desublimation); sublimation is the reverse, solid to gas. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: A process of deposition of calcium and other minerals on the surface of the cartilage is called.
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x: Deposition of calcium and other minerals that turns cartilage into bone is ossification. Off-topic (biology), moved.

1.s: Which type of chemical process is tarnishing of silver?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
1.x: Tarnishing of silver (black silver sulphide from H2S in air) is a form of corrosion. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: Which reaction demonstrate the chemical property of alcohols as reducing agent?
o: Reaction with sodium to release hydrogen
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Alcohols are oxidised to aldehydes or ketones, so they act as reducing agents (they are themselves oxidised); esterification, reaction with sodium and dehydration are not redox reactions of this kind. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: If two papers are kept very close to each other and wind is blown in between them, they would
1.src: APPSC AE (Environmental) Mains General Studies & Mental Abil
1.x: Air blown between the sheets moves fast and its pressure drops (Bernoulli's principle), so the higher outside pressure pushes the papers together. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: Which among the following is appropriate Phrasal verb for 'Loiter Aimlessly'?
1.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
1.x: 'Hang out' means to spend time idly or loiter; hold up = delay, keep on = continue, lay off = dismiss. Off-topic (English), moved.

1.s: Which gas is evolved when an acid reacts with a metal?
1.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
1.x: A metal reacting with an acid gives a salt and hydrogen gas (e.g. Zn + H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2). Off-topic (general science), moved.

1.s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are CORRECT for the processes involved in photosynthesis?

I. Absorption of light energy by chlorophyll

II. Oxidation of carbon dioxide to carbohydrates
1.src: APPSC Town Planning Building Overseers General Studies & Men
1.x: Photosynthesis begins with absorption of light by chlorophyll (I correct); carbon dioxide is reduced, not oxidised, to carbohydrate (II wrong) → Only I. Off-topic (biology), moved.

1.s: Apart from Sun light and Carbon Dioxide, the source for production of Oxygen through photosynthesis in plants is?
1.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
1.x: Plants split water in photosynthesis (photolysis); the oxygen released comes from water, not from CO2, air, chlorophyll or glucose. Off-topic (biology), moved.

1.s: To store potato chips for a longer period, the sealed packet of chips is normally filled with which gas?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
1.x: Chip packets are flushed with nitrogen, an unreactive gas, so the fats do not get oxidised (rancidity). Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: Formation of Carbon dioxide gas from Carbon and Oxygen is a/an?
1.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
1.x: Burning carbon in oxygen to CO2 gives out heat – an exothermic (combination) reaction. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: What is the main role of photosynthesis in plants?
o: To absorb water from the soil
To take in carbon dioxide and release helium
To transport vitamins through the stem
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P

1.s: Aerobic respiration process requires

1.x: Aerobic respiration breaks down glucose using oxygen (giving CO2, water, energy). Off-topic (biology), moved.

1.s: The production of tears when dust particles hit the human eye; is an example of which of the following?

1.s: What is a characteristic feature of a first-degree burn?
o: Minor epithelial damage, presence of redness
Partial thickness burn and scalds, may be painful
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
1.x: A first-degree (superficial) burn damages only the epidermis, with redness and pain; partial-thickness is second degree and full-thickness/necrosis third degree. Off-topic (first aid), moved.

1.s: Which one of the following is pure water?
1.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office

1.s: Transfer of pollen grains through wind is known as
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x: Anemophily is pollination by wind; hydrophily is by water, entomophily by insects and ornithophily by birds.

1.s: Who among the following determined the charge of electrons as 1.5924 x 10^-19 C?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
1.x: Robert Millikan's oil-drop experiment (1909-13) measured the electron's charge, about 1.59 x 10^-19 C in his 1913 result (now 1.602 x 10^-19 C).

1.s: Which of the following principles is used in the process of cooling air in air-conditioners?
1.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
1.x: Air-conditioners cool a room by circulating air: cooled air sinks and warm air rises to the unit – a convection current. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: When a semiconductor is heated, its resistance would
o: Resistance has no relation with temperature
1.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
1.x: A semiconductor has a negative temperature coefficient: heating frees more charge carriers, so its resistance decreases (a metal's would increase). Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: A person wonders how is it possible for insects to walk on water, human beings can't do it. In order to answer this question, we will have to refer to the concept of:
1.src: APPSC Town Planning Building Overseers General Studies & Men
1.x: Surface tension – the cohesive 'skin' of the water surface – supports light insects such as water striders. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: What is the freezing temperature used for preserving pork for long period
1.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Meat such as pork is stored long-term frozen at about −18°C (0°F) or below; 3–5°C is only chilling. Off-topic (food science), moved.

1.s: Amount of heat required to raise the temperature of one gram of substance by 1°C is called
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
1.x: The heat needed to raise the temperature of 1 g of a substance by 1°C is its specific heat. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: Why a glass bottle full of water breaks, if kept in a fridge?
o: The pressure in the fridge would be very high
When water solidifies, it expands in volume

1.x: Water expands by about 9% on freezing; the expanding ice exerts pressure that cracks the glass bottle. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: The electrical resistance of the insulators is
1.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
1.x: An ideal insulator offers (practically) infinitely high resistance to current, hence 'infinitely high' rather than merely 'high'. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: Which instrument is used to measure speed?
1.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
1.x: A tachometer measures speed (rotational speed of an engine, rpm); an ammeter measures current, a venturimeter flow rate. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: The instrument used to measure high temperatures
1.src: APSLPRB SI Paper-IV Final Written Exam 2017
1.x: A pyrometer measures very high temperatures (furnaces) from emitted radiation; a pedometer counts steps. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: If Mental Age of a Child is 6 and Physical Age is 10, the IQ of the child is?
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
1.x: IQ = mental age ÷ chronological age × 100 = 6 ÷ 10 × 100 = 60. Off-topic (psychology / mental ability), moved.

1.s: A projector for images of both opaque objects and transparencies is called an ______.
1.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
1.x: An epidiascope projects images of both opaque objects and transparencies (episcope + diascope); an anemometer measures wind speed. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: Which of the following substances is invariably formed, whenever an acid combines with a base?
1.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
1.x: An acid and a base always react to form a salt (and water). Off-topic science PYQ, moved.

1.s: A corked bottle full of water when frozen breaks because
o: The Volume of the water decreases on freezing
The volume of the water increases on freezing
Glass material develops strain of freezing

1.x: Water expands by about 9% on freezing; the expanding ice pushes on the glass and breaks the bottle. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: If a person goes down into a deep mine, his weight?
o: Depends on location of the mine
1.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
1.x: g falls with depth below the surface, so a person's weight decreases slightly in a deep mine. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: A hydrometer is used to measure?
1.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
1.x: A hydrometer measures the relative density (specific gravity) of liquids; humidity is measured by a hygrometer. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: When an air bubble at the bottom of a lake rises to the top, it will
o: Flattens into a dish like shape

1.s: A corked bottle full of water when frozen breaks because
o: The volume of the water decreases on freezing
The volume of the water increases on freezing
Glass material develops strain on freezing
1.x: Water expands on freezing; the ice pushes on the glass and breaks the bottle. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: Wood neither gaining or losing moisture content is called:
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
1.x: Wood that neither gains nor loses moisture is at its equilibrium moisture content (in balance with the surrounding humidity); the fibre saturation point is the stage when cell walls are saturated but cell cavities empty. No printed key. Off-topic (wood science), moved.

1.s: What happens to the weight of Iron when it rusts?
1.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
1.x: Rust is iron combined with oxygen and water (hydrated iron oxide), so the rusted iron weighs more. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.x: Supercooling is cooling a liquid below its freezing point without it solidifying. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: Out of the following, which would not indicate occurence of a chemical reaction?
1.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh

1.s: After taking out from the fridge, compared to an apple, water melon would retain the coolness for more time because?

It contains more water which has higher specific heat
It is more green in colour which does reflects atmospheric heat
It has thicker skin which would not allow penetration of heat
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
1.x: Watermelon contains more water, which has a high specific heat, so it takes longer to warm up. Off-topic (physics), moved.

o: The water will boil more and temperature of the water would fall
The Water will stop boiling and the temperature of the water would fall
The water will stop boiling and temperature of the water would rise
The water will boil more and the temperature of the water would rise

1.s: An 'aerosol' is a fine dispersion of
o: Tiny droplets of liquid in the air
Chalk and sand particles in water

1.x: An aerosol is a fine dispersion of liquid droplets (or solid particles) in air/gas, e.g. fog, mist, sprays. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

o: Melting point has no relation with pressure

The boiling point increases and freezing point decreases.
Both the boiling point and the freezing point increase.
Both the boiling point and freezing point decrease.

1.x: A dissolved salt raises the boiling point and lowers the freezing point of water (colligative properties). Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP

1.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017

1.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var

1.x: Stars twinkle because of atmospheric refraction by turbulent air layers of changing density. Off-topic (physics), moved.

In the bottom most row of the periodic table

1.x: A fuse melts and breaks the circuit when an excessive (heavy) current flows, protecting appliances. Off-topic (physics), moved.
