xa: APCERT: coalition of CSIRTs from **13 economies**; first conference **March 2002, Tokyo**.
The Cyber Diplomacy Division is the nodal point on cyber security, **data protection**, cybercrime and **internet governance**.
India is also in the US-led **Counter Ransomware Initiative** and the **Quad Senior Cyber Group**.

31.s: Which working group does India lead under the US-led Counter Ransomware Initiative?
31.x: India leads the Resilience Working Group of the Counter Ransomware Initiative.

31.s: CERT-In's exercise 'Synergy' under the Counter Ransomware Initiative involved how many countries?
31.x: Synergy was conducted for 13 countries.

31.s: Where was the first APCERT conference held in March 2002?
31.x: APCERT's first conference was held in Tokyo in March 2002.

31.s: Which of the following is one of the five pillars of the Colombo Security Conclave?
31.x: Cyber security is one of the five pillars of the Colombo Security Conclave.

31.s: Which country leads the Counter Ransomware Initiative, launched in 2021, in which India leads the Resilience Working Group?
31.x: The Counter Ransomware Initiative is US-led (2021); India leads its Resilience Working Group.

31.s: APCERT, of which India is a member, brings together the CSIRTs of how many economies?
31.x: APCERT has CSIRTs of 13 economies; its first conference was in Tokyo in March 2002.

31.s: Which of the following groupings has a Senior Cyber Group for cybersecurity partnership with India?
31.x: The Quad has a Senior Cyber Group under its cybersecurity partnership.

31.s: What score did India get in the ITU Global Cybersecurity Index 2024?
31.x: India scored 98.49 and was strong in all five pillars; the 2024 Index uses tiers, not numerical ranks.
xa: ⚠ GCI 2020 = rank **10**; GCI 2024 = **Tier-1**, no ranks.
The GCI is published by the **ITU**.

31.s: India was ranked 10th in which edition of the ITU Global Cybersecurity Index?
31.x: India was ranked 10th in the GCI 2020. The GCI 2024 shifted from numerical ranks to tiers.
31.tq: Numerical-year discrimination between the earlier rank-based edition and the later tier-based edition.
xs: India was ranked **10th** in **GCI 2020** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**GCI 2024** has no ranks; it uses **tiers**, and India is **Tier-1 "Role Modelling"**.
xa: GCI 2024 score: **98.49**, strong in all **five pillars**.
The index is brought out by the **ITU** (International Telecommunication Union).

31.s: The Andhra Pradesh Cyber Security Policy 2017, implemented by APTS, has how many verticals?
31.x: It has four verticals, including securing critical government infrastructure and capacity building.
xa: Telangana's state campaign: **#OnlineButUnafraid** for women journalists.
National counterpart: **NCSP 2013**, vision of a **secure and resilient cyberspace**.

31.s: Into which of the following does the ITU Global Cybersecurity Index 2024 group countries?
31.x: GCI 2024 uses tiers, not ranks; India's rank of 10 was in GCI 2020.

31.s: What is the name of India's tier in the ITU Global Cybersecurity Index 2024?
31.x: India is in Tier-1 'Role Modelling' with a score of 98.49.

31.s: Which agency implements the Andhra Pradesh Cyber Security Policy 2017?
31.x: The AP Cyber Security Policy 2017 is implemented by AP Technology Services (APTS), not CERT-In.

32.s: In 2017, The Supreme Court of India ruled that Right to Privacy is 'intrinsic to life and personal liberty' and is inherently protected under ____, and as a part of the freedom guaranteed by Part III of the Constitution.
32.src: APPSC AEE General Studies & Mental Abilities 2023
32.x: In K.S. Puttaswamy v Union of India (2017) the Supreme Court held privacy protected as an intrinsic part of life and personal liberty under Article 21 and as part of the freedoms of Part III. Articles 20, 22 and 23 deal with conviction, detention and forced labour.

32.s: In which land mark case filed by the following person, Supreme Court held that the right to privacy in intrinsic part of right to life and personal liberty granted under Article 21 of the Constitution?
32.src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains P
32.x: The 2017 privacy case was filed by Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd); it overruled M.P. Sharma (1954) and Kharak Singh (1962) insofar as they denied privacy. PUCL (1997) dealt with telephone interception.

32.s: Right to Privacy is contained in:
32.x: Privacy is part of the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21, as held in K.S. Puttaswamy (2017).

32.s: Right to Privacy is protected as an intrinsic part of Right to Life and Personal Liberty. Which of the following in the Constitution of India correctly and appropriately imply the above statement? Indian Polity: Constitutional Framework PMF IAS IP – 14
o: Article 14 and the provisions under the 42nd Amendment to the Constitution
Article 17 and the Directive Principles of State Policy in Part IV
Article 21 and freedom guaranteed in Part III
32.x: Puttaswamy (2017) held privacy protected as an intrinsic part of life and personal liberty under Article 21 and the freedoms of Part III. Articles 14, 17, 24, the DPSPs and the 42nd/44th Amendments are not the basis.

32.s: 'Right to Privacy' is protected under which Article of the Constitution of India?
32.x: A nine-judge bench in Puttaswamy (2017) unanimously recognised privacy as a Fundamental Right flowing from Article 21 and other Part III freedoms.

32.s: Article 21 of Indian Constitution secures
o: Right to life, personal liberty and right to privacy
32.x: Article 21 secures life and personal liberty, and Puttaswamy (2017) held privacy intrinsic to them, so option 4 is complete; options 1-3 each leave something out.

32.s: How many judges unanimously decided K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India, which recognised privacy as intrinsic to life and liberty?
32.x: A unanimous nine-judge bench held privacy protected under Article 21 and Part III.
xa: Date: **24 August 2017**.
Overruled **M.P. Sharma (1954)** and **Kharak Singh (1962)** to the extent they denied privacy.
Follow-up: the **DPDP Act 2023** with a **Data Protection Board**.

32.s: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India overruled M.P. Sharma and Kharak Singh to the extent that those decisions had done which of the following?
o: Recognised proportionality as the sole test for all restrictions
Denied the existence of privacy as a protected constitutional interest
Declared education to be a Directive Principle
32.x: Puttaswamy overruled M.P. Sharma (1954) and Kharak Singh (1962) insofar as they denied privacy as a constitutional protection.
32.tq: Focus on the limited extent of overruling instead of treating the earlier judgments as wholly erased.
xs: Puttaswamy overruled them to the extent they **denied privacy** as a protected constitutional interest — so option **(2)** is correct.
**M.P. Sharma** was **1954**; **Kharak Singh** was **1962**.
xa: Yet **Kharak Singh v State of UP (1962)** is also cited for early recognition of privacy concerns under **Art. 21**.
**Gobind v State of MP (1975)** recognised privacy as part of personal liberty.
Puttaswamy: **nine-judge**, unanimous, **24 August 2017**.

32.s: A government measure restricts personal data without any supporting law, although it claims to pursue a public objective. Which requirement of the privacy test is most clearly absent?
32.x: The legality requirement demands that an intrusion into privacy be supported by a law. A claimed public objective cannot substitute for the existence of legal authority.
32.tq: Apply the first step of the privacy test by asking whether the restriction has a legal basis.
xs: With no supporting law, the first test — **Legality** (a law) — is missing; option **(2)** is correct.
A public objective would satisfy the **legitimate aim** test, so option 1 is not what is absent.
The three tests are **legality**, **legitimate aim / need** and **proportionality**.
xa: These tests were later applied to **Aadhaar (2018)**.
**NAFRS** (facial recognition) runs **without a statute**, so it is questioned under the Puttaswamy tests.
Any state surveillance must meet the **Puttaswamy tests**.

32.s: Which of the following case–proposition pairs is correctly matched?
o: Kharak Singh v State of UP – Privacy recognised as a Fundamental Right
Gobind v State of MP – Privacy recognised as part of personal liberty
Puttaswamy v Union of India – Early recognition of privacy concerns under Article 21
Kharak Singh v State of UP – Informational privacy affirmed
32.x: Gobind v State of MP (1975) treated privacy as part of personal liberty. Kharak Singh (1962) was overruled by Puttaswamy insofar as it denied privacy, so it did not recognise privacy as a Fundamental Right. Puttaswamy (2017) was not an early case: its nine judges unanimously held privacy a Fundamental Right under Article 21.

32.s: In which case were safeguards on interception of communications in India laid down?
o: Kharak Singh v State of UP (1962)
K.S. Puttaswamy v Union of India (2017)
Shreya Singhal v Union of India (2015)
32.x: Interception safeguards come from PUCL v Union of India (1997), not Kharak Singh.
xa: **Kharak Singh (1962)** is an early privacy case under **Art. 21**.
**Pegasus** committee: **Justice R.V. Raveendran**; malware on **5 of 29** phones.

32.s: On which date was K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India decided?
32.x: The nine-judge Puttaswamy judgment came on 24 August 2017; 26 September 2018 is the Aadhaar judgment.

32.s: Which 1975 case held privacy to be part of personal liberty?
32.x: Gobind v State of MP (1975) treated privacy as part of personal liberty.

32.s: Under which Article of the Constitution did the Supreme Court in K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017) place the right to privacy?
32.x: Puttaswamy held privacy to be intrinsic to life and personal liberty under Article 21 and Part III.

32.s: Which of the adopted following a law on data protection and privacy for its citizens known as 'General Data Protection Regulation' in April 2016 and started implementation of it from 25th May, 2018?
32.x: The European Union adopted the GDPR in April 2016 and applied it from 25 May 2018, replacing the 1995 Data Protection Directive.

32.s: Which of the following adopted a law on data protection and privacy for its citizens known as 'General Data Protection Regulation' in April 2016 and started implementation of it from 25th May, 2018?
32.x: The European Union adopted the GDPR in April 2016 and applied it from 25 May 2018, replacing the 1995 Data Protection Directive.

32.s: Which of the following is true of the Right to Be Forgotten as understood in India?
o: Applies only to biometric data collected by UIDAI
Limits name-based searches without necessarily erasing judicial records
Automatically cancels the judgment of a court
Prohibits every search involving the person's name
32.x: The Indian understanding of RTBF does not erase judicial records; it can limit name-based searches in appropriate circumstances.
xa: Delhi HC in **Laksh Vir Singh Yadav v UoI**: framework to de-index name searches of **acquitted persons**.
In India RTBF flows from **Art. 21** (Puttaswamy) and is **not absolute**.
Origin: **Google Spain v. AEPD (2014)**.

32.s: Under which Article of the GDPR is the Right to be Forgotten formalised as the 'Right to Erasure'?
32.x: The GDPR's Right to Erasure is Article 17; RTBF originated in Google Spain v. AEPD (2014), and the DPDP Act gives a Right to Erasure under Section 12.
xa: ⚠ Right to Erasure = GDPR **Art. 17**; DPDP **Sec. 12**; privacy itself = Indian **Art. 21**.
In India RTBF is part of privacy under **Art. 21** (Puttaswamy) but **not absolute**; no standalone law.

32.s: The Right to Be Forgotten began with which case?
o: K.S. Puttaswamy v Union of India (2017)
32.x: The Right to Be Forgotten began in Google Spain v AEPD (2014).

32.s: The GDPR replaced the EU Data Protection Directive of which year?
32.x: The GDPR replaced the 1995 Directive.

32.s: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) of the European Union was implemented from which date?
32.x: The EU GDPR, adopted in April 2016, was implemented from 25 May 2018.
32.tq: Use the precise implementation date rather than the adoption date.
xs: **GDPR** was implemented from **25 May 2018** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was adopted by the **European Union** in **April 2016**.
xa: GDPR formalised the **Right to Erasure** in **Art. 17**.
⚠ **26 Sep 2018** is India's **Aadhaar** judgment — do not confuse.

32.s: Which of the following correctly contrasts penalties under the EU GDPR and India's DPDP Act, 2023?
o: GDPR provides administrative fines and lets member states add criminal penalties; the DPDP Act provides financial penalties only
GDPR provides criminal penalties only; the DPDP Act provides imprisonment
GDPR has no fines; the DPDP Act provides both fines and imprisonment
32.x: The GDPR itself prescribes administrative fines (up to EUR 20 million or 4% of global turnover) and lets member states lay down other, including criminal, penalties; the DPDP Act, 2023 provides financial penalties only.

32.s: Who dissented in the 4:1 Aadhaar judgment of 26 September 2018?
32.x: The five-judge Bench decided 4:1, with Justice D.Y. Chandrachud dissenting.
xa: Upheld: Aadhaar Act and passage as **Money Bill**; mandatory for welfare (**Sec. 7**); **PAN/ITR linking**.
Struck down: **Sec. 57** (private entities); bank-account and **SIM** linking.

32.s: Which Aadhaar linking was upheld in the Aadhaar judgment (2018)?
o: Mandatory linking with both bank accounts and SIMs
32.x: PAN/ITR linking under Section 139AA was upheld; mandatory linking with bank accounts and mobile SIMs was struck down.

32.s: Which of the following was NOT upheld in the Aadhaar judgment (2018)?
32.x: Section 57 private-entity use was struck down; the Act, welfare use and PAN/ITR linking were upheld.

32.s: How many judges delivered the Aadhaar judgment of 26 September 2018?
32.x: The Aadhaar bench had 5 judges (4:1), unlike the 9-judge Puttaswamy bench.

32.s: Which body prepared the 2018 draft personal data protection Bill?
32.x: The Justice B.N. Srikrishna Committee drafted the 2018 Bill (2017-18), before the 2019 PDP Bill, its 2022 withdrawal and the 2023 DPDP Act.
xa: **2021**: JPC report with **93 amendments**, covering personal and non-personal data.
**2012**: **Justice A.P. Shah** Group of Experts on Privacy.
DPDP Act assent: **11 Aug 2023**.

32.s: The 2021 Joint Parliamentary Committee report on the Personal Data Protection Bill proposed how many amendments?
32.x: The 2021 JPC report proposed 93 amendments and covered both personal and non-personal data; the Bill was withdrawn in 2022.
xa: After withdrawal, a narrower **DPDP draft** was released; the **DPDP Act** passed in **2023**.
The PDP Bill traces to the **Justice B.N. Srikrishna Committee** (MeitY).

32.s: With which of the following is the Kris Gopalakrishnan Committee associated?
32.x: The Kris Gopalakrishnan Committee dealt with non-personal data; A.P. Shah with privacy, Srikrishna with the PDP Bill and A.K. Bhargava with net neutrality.
xa: ⚠ Trap: an "A.P. Shah Committee (2015)" on net neutrality is wrong — that was **A.K. Bhargava**.
The A.P. Shah group worked under the **Planning Commission**.

32.s: In which year was the Personal Data Protection Bill, 2019 withdrawn?
32.x: The 2019 Bill was withdrawn in 2022, before the DPDP Act of 2023.

32.s: Who headed the 2012 Group of Experts on Privacy?
32.x: Justice A.P. Shah headed the 2012 Group of Experts on Privacy.

32.s: Who headed the 2015 DoT committee on net neutrality?
32.x: A.K. Bhargava headed the net neutrality committee; A.P. Shah headed the privacy experts group.

32.s: In which year did the Digital Personal Data Protection Act receive Presidential assent?
32.x: The DPDP Act received assent on 11 August 2023, after the 2019 Bill was withdrawn in 2022.

32.s: In which year was the Personal Data Protection Bill referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee?
32.x: The PDP Bill, 2019 was sent to a JPC in 2019; the JPC reported in 2021 with 93 amendments.

32.s: Which kind of data is excluded from the DPDP Act, 2023?
o: Data of foreign entities offering goods in India
32.x: The DPDP Act excludes non-personal data, though it covers entities outside India offering goods or services in India.

32.s: Under the DPDP Act, 2023, who is the Data Principal for a child under 18?
32.x: For a child under 18, the parent or guardian is treated as the Data Principal, not the Data Fiduciary.
xa: GDPR equivalents: **Data Subject / Data Controller**.
**Consent Manager**: registered entity through which a principal gives, manages and withdraws consent.

32.s: Which of the following is NOT an additional obligation of a Significant Data Fiduciary?
o: Appointment of a Data Protection Officer in India
Automatic exemption from all consent requirements
32.x: A Significant Data Fiduciary must appoint a Data Protection Officer in India, appoint an independent auditor and undertake impact assessment. It does not receive an automatic exemption from consent requirements.
32.tq: Find the option that reverses an additional compliance duty into an exemption.
xs: **Automatic exemption from all consent requirements** is not an SDF obligation — so option **(3)** is correct.
SDF extra duties: appoint a **DPO in India**, an **independent auditor**, and conduct an **impact assessment**.
xa: SDFs are notified by the Centre on **volume, sensitivity and risk**.
Penalty for breaching SDF duties: up to **Rs 150 crore**.

32.s: Under the DPDP Act, 2023, what is a Consent Manager?
o: A government officer who investigates cybercrime
A registered entity through which a Data Principal gives, manages and withdraws consent
An auditor appointed only by a Significant Data Fiduciary
A tribunal hearing appeals from the Board
32.x: A Consent Manager is a registered entity enabling a Data Principal to give, manage and withdraw consent.
32.tq: Exact-term discrimination based on function and institutional role.
xs: A **Consent Manager** is a **registered entity** through which a Data Principal **gives, manages and withdraws consent** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Appeals from the Board go to **TDSAT**, not a Consent Manager.
xa: Consent Manager provisions come into force in **November 2026** (12 months after the Rules).
Full compliance: **May 2027** (18 months).

32.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the DPDP Act, 2023 and the GDPR?
o: The DPDP Act covers only digital personal data, whereas the GDPR covers all personal data.
Both frameworks use the term 'Data Fiduciary' for the entity deciding the purposes of processing.
The DPDP Act provides for financial penalties only.
Data portability is an explicit GDPR right but not a statutory right under the DPDP Act.
32.x: The GDPR uses 'Data Controller'; 'Data Fiduciary' is DPDP Act terminology.
xa: DPDP maximum penalty: **Rs 250 crore**.
Regulator: **Data Protection Board of India** vs a **DPA in each member state**.

32.s: What is the GDPR term for the DPDP Act's 'Data Fiduciary'?
32.x: A Data Fiduciary decides purpose and means of processing, like the GDPR's Data Controller.

32.s:
Consider the following statements about the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023:
1. It covers only digital personal data.
2. It also applies to foreign entities offering goods or services in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
32.x: The DPDP Act covers only digital personal data and also reaches foreign entities offering goods or services in India.

32.s: Which of the following is NOT a recognised right of a Data Principal under the DPDP framework?
o: Right to impose criminal penalties on a Data Fiduciary
32.x: The listed rights include information and access, correction, erasure, grievance redress, withdrawal of consent and nomination. A Data Principal does not impose criminal penalties on a Data Fiduciary.
32.tq: Identify the outsider by separating an individual data right from an enforcement power.
xs: There is no right to **impose criminal penalties** on a Data Fiduciary — so option **(1)** is correct.
Rights: **information/access**, **correction, erasure**, grievance redress, **withdrawal of consent**, **nomination**.
xa: DPDP penalties are **financial only**, up to **Rs 250 crore**.
**Data portability** is not a statutory right under DPDP (explicit in GDPR).

32.s: The right to erasure of a Data Principal is in which section of the DPDP Act?
32.x: Erasure is in Section 12 of the DPDP Act; under the GDPR it is Article 17.

32.s: Which of the following is a duty of a Data Principal under the DPDP Act?
32.x: Data Principals must not give false information, impersonate or file frivolous complaints.

32.s:
Consider the following statements about children's data under the DPDP Act, 2023:
1. Verifiable parental consent is needed for persons below 18.
2. Targeted advertising at children is barred.
3. Behavioural monitoring of children is permitted.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
32.x: Parental consent is needed below 18 and tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted ads are barred, so statement 3 is false.

32.s: Under the DPDP framework, below what age is verifiable parental consent required?
32.x: Verifiable parental consent is needed below 18 years; tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted ads aimed at children are banned.
xa: Penalty for breach of **children's data** obligations: up to **Rs 200 crore**.
**DPDP Rules** were notified on **14 November 2025**.
**Consent Manager** provisions come into force in **November 2026**.

32.s: Which of the following receives no exemption under the DPDP Act, 2023?
32.x: Journalism gets no exemption; notified State agencies, research, archiving and statistics can be exempted.

32.s: Which section of the DPDP Act, 2023 contains the 'legitimate uses' that allow the State to process personal data without consent?
32.x: Section 7 covers legitimate uses; Section 17 lets the Centre exempt notified State agencies on grounds of sovereignty, security and public order.
xa: **Startups** can be exempted; **journalism** gets no exemption.
Max penalty for security safeguard failure: **Rs 250 crore**.
Appeals from the **Data Protection Board** lie to **TDSAT**.

32.s: Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act was amended by which provision of the DPDP Act, 2023?
32.x: Section 44(3) of the DPDP Act amended Section 8(1)(j), letting authorities refuse all personal information and removing the public-interest override.
xa: Petition by **Venkatesh Nayak**; challenges **referred to a Constitution Bench**.
In **Aug 2026** the SC asked whether the law is "**crippling RTI**".

32.s: What did the DPDP Act's amendment of RTI Section 8(1)(j) remove?
32.x: Section 44(3) lets all personal information be refused and removes the public-interest override.

32.s: Which section of the DPDP Act provides for exemption of notified State agencies?
32.x: Section 17 lets the Centre exempt notified State agencies; Section 7 covers legitimate uses.

32.s: In August 2026, to which bench was the challenge to the DPDP Act's amendment of RTI Section 8(1)(j) referred?
o: A Full Bench of the Delhi High Court
32.x: The challenge to Sec. 44(3) amending RTI Sec. 8(1)(j) was referred to a Constitution Bench in August 2026.

32.s: Under the DPDP framework, what is the maximum penalty for breach of obligations regarding children's data?
32.x: Children's data obligations carry up to ₹200 crore; additional SDF duties ₹150 crore and residual breaches ₹50 crore.
xa: Highest: **₹250 crore** for failure of **security safeguards**.
DPDP penalties are **financial only**; GDPR adds criminal ones in some states.

32.s: What is the maximum penalty for failure to take reasonable security safeguards under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act?
32.x: Failure of reasonable security safeguards may attract a maximum penalty of ₹250 crore.
32.tq: Numerical recall using the graded penalty figures as close distractors.
xs: Failure of reasonable security safeguards attracts up to **₹250 crore** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**₹200 crore** = children's data; **₹150 crore** = SDF duties; **₹50 crore** = residual breach.
xa: ⚠ **250 – 200 – 150 – 50** crore = security safeguards – children – SDFs – residual.
Data Principals' false information: up to **₹10,000**.

32.s: Where do appeals against decisions of the Data Protection Board of India lie?
32.x: Appeals lie to TDSAT; the Board is headquartered in New Delhi and its members are appointed by the Central Government.
xa: The Board is an **adjudicatory** body.
Board provisions came into force **immediately** on **14 November 2025** Rules.

32.s: Who appoints the members of the Data Protection Board of India?
32.x: The Centre appoints Board members; appeals lie to TDSAT.

32.s: What is the maximum penalty for breach of Significant Data Fiduciary duties under the DPDP Act?
32.x: SDF breaches carry up to Rs 150 crore in the 250-200-150-50 crore ladder.

32.s: What is the maximum penalty for a Data Principal breaching her duties under the DPDP Act?
32.x: Breach of Data Principal duties attracts up to Rs 10,000.

32.s: Where is the headquarters of the Data Protection Board of India?
32.x: The Data Protection Board, an adjudicatory body under the DPDP Act, has its headquarters in New Delhi.

32.s: What is the maximum penalty for a residual breach of the DPDP Act, 2023, not covered by a specific head?
32.x: The penalty ladder is 250-200-150-50 crore; residual breaches carry up to Rs 50 crore.

32.s: "Pegasus Allegations" Committee, constituted by the Supreme Court, is headed by...
32.src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022
32.x: On 27 Oct 2021 the Supreme Court (CJI N.V. Ramana) set up an independent technical committee on the Pegasus allegations overseen by retired SC judge Justice R.V. Raveendran.

32.s: When were the final Digital Personal Data Protection Rules notified?
32.x: The final DPDP Rules were notified on 14 November 2025; 3 January 2025 was the date of release of the draft Rules.
32.tq: Distinguish the draft-release date from the final-notification date.
xs: Final **DPDP Rules** were notified on **14 November 2025** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**3 Jan 2025** = draft Rules; **11 Aug 2023** = Act's assent; **May 2027** = full compliance.
xa: Phases: Board **immediately**; **Consent Manager** in **November 2026**; full compliance **May 2027**.
Rules require **plain-language notices** and **purpose limitation**.

32.s: Which of the following sets of practices is in line with the DPDP Rules?
o: Clear and specific consent, plain-language notices and purpose limitation
Consent without information, unrestricted collection and unlimited reuse
Implied consent, technical notices and indefinite retention
Anonymous consent, no retention controls and compulsory foreign storage
32.x: The Rules require clear, specific and informed consent, plain-language notices, purpose limitation, data minimisation and retention controls.
32.tq: Select the option containing the complete set of positive compliance practices.
xs: **Clear and specific consent, plain-language notices and purpose limitation** fit the Rules — so option **(1)** is correct.
Unrestricted collection, indefinite retention and no retention controls all contradict **data minimisation** and **retention controls**.
xa: Consent must also be **informed**.
Full operational compliance: **May 2027**.

32.s: Who supervised the Supreme Court-appointed technical committee in the Pegasus matter?
32.x: Justice R.V. Raveendran supervised the committee, which found malware on 5 of 29 phones but could not conclusively link it to Pegasus.
xa: Safeguards on interception: **PUCL v UoI (1997)**.

32.s: Under the DPDP Rules notified on 14 November 2025, by when is full operational compliance due?
32.x: Full compliance is due 18 months after notification, in May 2027; Consent Manager provisions come in November 2026.
xa: Draft Rules: **3 Jan 2025**.
Fiduciary duties: **purpose limitation**, **data minimisation**, **retention controls**.

32.s: What do India's first national standards for cloud, data centres and ethical AI focus on?
32.x: The standards focus on bias, data sovereignty and privacy and are linked to the DPDP Act; spectrum auction pricing is not among them.

32.s: When did RBI issue the mandate requiring all payment-system data to be stored only in India?
32.x: The RBI's April 2018 mandate required all payment-system data to be stored only in India.
xa: DPDP cross-border: **blacklist (negative-list)** — allowed except to countries the Centre restricts.
Critics call the DPDP approach **light-touch**.
⚠ DPDP = **blacklist**; GDPR = **whitelist / adequacy**.

32.s: How does the DPDP Act treat transfer of personal data outside India?
o: Permitted only to countries approved by the RBI
Permitted except to countries restricted by the Central Government
32.x: The DPDP Act follows a blacklist (negative-list) approach: transfers are allowed unless the Central Government restricts particular countries.
xa: Critics call the approach **light-touch**.
RBI's separate rule (**April 2018**): payment-system data stored **only in India**.

32.s: Under the DPDP Rules 2025, from when do the Consent Manager provisions apply?
32.x: Consent Manager provisions apply from November 2026; full compliance is due by May 2027.

32.s: When were the draft DPDP Rules released?
32.x: The draft came on 3 January 2025 and the final Rules on 14 November 2025.

32.s: The Supreme Court's Pegasus committee found malware on how many of the 29 phones examined?
32.x: Malware was found on 5 of 29 phones, though not clearly Pegasus.

32.s: How does the GDPR regulate cross-border data transfer?
32.x: GDPR uses a whitelist/adequacy model; the DPDP Act uses a blacklist.

32.s: AP Police's AI4AP pilot, which raises DPDP issues, covers which districts?

35.s:
Assertion (A) : Artificial satellites are always launched from the earth in the eastward direction.
Reason (R) : The earth rotates from west to east and so the Satellite attains the escape velocity.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, (R) is not a correct
35.x:
Official key / most books: (c) A true, R false. Strictly: A is also false, since not all satellites go eastward (polar/SSO launches go south; Israel launches westward).
Eastward launches use the Earth's west-to-east spin, so the key takes A as true. R is false: that boost does not give escape velocity, and an orbiting satellite never reaches it.

35.s: What is the full form of GTO in launch terminology?

xa: **GEO** = GSO over the equator, so the satellite stays **fixed in the sky**.

35.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about orbits?

GTO is an elliptical transfer orbit with its apogee near 36,000 km.

35.x: Apogee is the farthest point of an orbit; perigee is the nearest.
xa: **SSO** is near-polar and passes each place at the same local solar time.
**Eastward** launches gain Earth's rotational speed.
Polar/SSO launches go **southward** — hence the **Kulasekarapattinam** site.

passes over a given place at the same local solar time

36.s: Where are cryogenic engines (liquid hydrogen + liquid oxygen) mainly used?
o: Military missiles kept ready for long periods
36.x: Cryogenic propulsion is used in rocket upper stages (and was used on the space shuttle) because of its very high specific impulse (~450 s). Its low-density LH2 needs huge tanks and cannot be stored long, so it is unsuited to military missiles; attitude-control thrusters use hypergolic propellants that ignite on contact; sounding rockets use solid motors.
xs: Cryogenic (LH2 + LOX) engines are mainly used in **rocket upper stages** — option **(1)** (UPSC **1995**, UPPSC **1993**).
Low-density LH2 (**0.071 g/ml**) needs huge tanks and cannot be stored long, so they are **unsuited to military missiles**.
**Hypergolic** propellants (ignite on contact) are the ones ideal for **spacecraft manoeuvring**.
xa: They were also used on the **space shuttle** — **Discovery's** tanks held LH2 + LOX.
Isp ~**450 s** — highest; exhaust only **water vapour**.
Indian examples: **CE-7.5** (GSLV Mk II upper stage) and **CE-20** (LVM3 **C25** upper stage).

36.s: At about what temperature is liquid hydrogen stored in a cryogenic engine?
36.x: LH2 (the fuel) is stored at about -253°C and LOX (the oxidiser) at about -183°C; the exhaust is only water vapour.
xa: Cryogenic specific impulse ~**450 s** — the **highest** of all propellant categories.
LH2 density is only **0.071 g/ml** → huge tanks; unsuited to **military missiles**.
Used in **rocket upper stages**/space shuttle; **Discovery's** tanks held LH2 + LOX (UPPSC **2006**).
The propellant pair was asked in **UPPSC 2004**.

36.s: Which propellant category is correctly matched with its characteristic?
o: Solid — high initial thrust but cannot normally be throttled or stopped
Hybrid — cannot be stopped or restarted
Hypergolic — requires an external ignition system at every start
Cryogenic — least efficient but simplest to handle
36.x: Solid propellants provide high initial thrust but generally cannot be throttled or stopped. Hypergolic propellants ignite on contact, hybrids can be stopped or restarted, and cryogenic systems are highly efficient but complex.
36.tq: Compare the operational feature of each propellant category instead of relying on the category name alone.
xs: **Solid** propellants give **high initial thrust** but **cannot be throttled or stopped** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Hybrid** (solid fuel + liquid oxidiser) **can be stopped/restarted**, so option (2) reverses the fact.
**Hypergolic** propellants **ignite on contact** — no external ignition needed, so option (3) is wrong.
**Cryogenic** (LH2 + LOX) is the **most efficient** but **complex**, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: Solid example: **HTPB**, used in the **PSLV/GSLV first stage** and **S200**; Isp ~**260 s**.
**Earth-storable liquids** (UH25/N2O4) are **throttleable and restartable**; Isp ~**290-320 s**.
**Semi-cryogenic** (kerosene + LOX) is **dense, cheaper and non-toxic**.
⚠ **Cryogenic** = LH2 + LOX; **Semi-cryogenic** = kerosene + LOX; **Hypergolic** = ignite on contact.

36.s: Which of the following is an earth-storable liquid propellant combination?
36.x: UH25 and N2O4 are listed as earth-storable liquid propellants. Refined kerosene and LOX are semi-cryogenic, while LH2 and LOX are cryogenic.
36.tq: Separate earth-storable liquid propellants from cryogenic and semi-cryogenic combinations.
xs: **UH25 and N2O4** is an **earth-storable liquid** combination — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Refined kerosene + LOX** is **semi-cryogenic**; **LH2 + LOX** is **cryogenic**.
**Solid fuel + liquid oxidiser** is a **hybrid** propellant.
xa: Other earth-storable liquids: **hydrazine, MMH, UDMH**; they are **throttleable and restartable** (Isp ~**290-320 s**).
ISRO's **Vikas** engine runs on **UH25 + N2O4** (PSLV 2nd stage, GSLV 2nd stage and strap-ons, LVM3 **L110** core).
**Hypergolic** = hydrazine family + **N2O4** — ignites on contact but is **highly toxic**.

36.s: Why are hydrazine-family propellants combined with N2O4 called hypergolic?
o: Are non-toxic and suitable for large reusable boosters
Require cryogenic storage and have the highest specific impulse
Ignite on contact and are useful for spacecraft manoeuvring
36.x: Hypergolic propellants ignite on contact and are useful for spacecraft manoeuvring, although they are highly toxic.
36.tq: Use the defining property of hypergolic propellants to identify the correct application.
xs: Hydrazine-family + **N2O4** propellants are hypergolic because they **ignite on contact** and are **useful for spacecraft manoeuvring** — option **(4)**.
They are **highly toxic**, so option (1) "non-toxic" is wrong; **semi-cryogenic** kerosene + LOX is the non-toxic one.
**Cryogenic storage and highest Isp** describe **LH2 + LOX** (~**450 s**), not hypergolics.
xa: Hydrazine, **MMH** and **UDMH** are also listed as **earth-storable** liquids — throttleable and **restartable**.
**Solid** (HTPB) motors are the ones that **cannot be throttled or stopped**.
⚠ **Hypergolic** = ignite on contact; **Cryogenic** = LH2 + LOX; **Semi-cryogenic** = kerosene + LOX.

36.s: What is the main advantage of a scramjet over a conventional rocket during atmospheric flight?
o: It operates with subsonic airflow at speeds below Mach 2.
It eliminates the need for fuel during hypersonic flight.
It uses oxygen from the atmosphere, thereby reducing the weight of onboard oxidiser.
It uses a compressor to compress atmospheric air before combustion.
36.x: A scramjet uses oxygen from the atmosphere, so it need not carry the entire oxidiser required by a rocket. It still requires fuel and works with supersonic airflow.
36.tq: Use the function-based option; distinguish an air-breathing engine from a rocket.
xs: A scramjet uses **atmospheric oxygen**, so it **cuts onboard oxidiser weight** — option **(3)**.
It still needs **fuel**, so option (2) is wrong.
It burns in **supersonic** airflow at **Mach 5-6+** — subsonic combustion above **Mach 2** is a **ramjet**.
Compression comes from **forward speed**, **no compressor**, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: Challenge: **"a candle in a hurricane"**.
India became the **4th** country (after **US, Russia, China**) to demonstrate scramjet flight (ATV, **Aug 2016**).
DRDO's actively cooled scramjet combustor ran **20 minutes** on indigenous **endothermic hydrocarbon** fuel (May **2026**).

38.s: Besides communication payloads, GSAT-10 (2012) carried a payload for which system?
38.x: GSAT-10, launched on Ariane-5, carried communication and GAGAN payloads.

38.s: With which organisation does ISRO implement GAGAN?
38.x: GAGAN is an ISRO-Airports Authority of India system for civil aviation precision landing.

38.s: What does GAGAN stand for?
38.x: GAGAN = GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation; its ground stations send corrections for aviation.

39.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the Remote Sensing system?
39.x: The stages are energy source, radiation through the atmosphere, interaction with the target, recording, transmission/reception/processing, interpretation and application. 'Interaction of energy with minimisation' is not one.

39.s: Which of the following is NOT the application of remote sensing in disaster management?
39.x: Remote sensing is used for glacial lakes, wildfires and wind/cyclone tracking; 'hills management' is not a disaster application.

39.s: Remote Sensing uses which of the following in its applications?
39.x: Remote sensing measures reflected and emitted electromagnetic radiation from a distance; sonar uses sound, not EM waves.

39.s: Which of the following equipment is used to detect people trapped under rubble due to building collapse after earthquake?
39.x: Infrared (thermal) cameras detect the body heat of people trapped under rubble even when they cannot be seen.

39.s: What does GEOSS stand for?
o: Global Earth Observation System of Systems
Geo Stationery Environmental Observation Satellite System
Group on Earth Observation Satellite System
39.x: GEOSS = Global Earth Observation System of Systems, built by the intergovernmental Group on Earth Observations (GEO).

39.s: What type of remote sensing platform is most suitable for detailed localized disaster damage assessment?
39.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Mains Paper-I General Studies & M
39.x: A UAV (drone) flies low and on demand, giving very high-resolution images of a small area, so it suits detailed localised damage assessment; aircraft and satellites cover wider areas.

39.s: Which one of the following most appropriately describes remote sensing?
o: Preparation of maps only through manual surveying
Measurement of only the chemical composition of rocks by direct sampling
Recording of atmospheric pressure exclusively through ground instruments
Collection of information about the Earth without physical contact, using reflected or emitted electromagnetic radiation
39.x: Remote sensing obtains information about the Earth without physical contact by detecting reflected or emitted electromagnetic radiation.
39.tq: Use the precise definition and eliminate options that restrict the concept to one application or instrument.
xs: Remote sensing is the **collection of information about the Earth without physical contact**, using **reflected or emitted electromagnetic radiation** — option **(4)**.
Manual surveying, direct rock sampling and ground pressure gauges all involve contact or on-site measurement, so they are not remote sensing.
xa: Chain: **energy source** → radiation through atmosphere → **interaction with target** → sensor recording → **transmission, reception and processing** → interpretation → application.
**Passive** sensors use sunlight or emitted heat; **active** sensors send their own pulse (e.g. **RISAT SAR**, **LiDAR**).
In India, data are processed at **NRSC, Hyderabad** (nodal).

39.s: In a remote sensing system, which stage comes right after recording by the sensor?
39.x: The stages run: energy source, atmosphere, interaction with target, recording, then transmission, reception and processing, interpretation, application.

39.s: Remote sensing gathers information about a target without which of the following?
39.x: Remote sensing works from a distance without physical contact, so physical sampling is not one of its stages.

39.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about Airborne Laser Terrain Mapping (ALTM)?

I. It is a cheap, fast accurate way of creating 3D digital picture of the earth surface and objects on it.

II. Currently it is mainly used for mapping or survey application
39.x: Airborne Laser Terrain Mapping is airborne LiDAR: a fast, accurate and cost-effective way to build a 3D digital picture of the ground (I), used today mainly for mapping and survey (II). So both are correct.

39.s: In the visible spectrum, the colour having the shortest wavelength is :
39.x: In the visible spectrum violet has the shortest wavelength and red the longest.

39.s: Which of the following is a popular remote sensing method that used light in the form of a pulsed laser to measure ranges (distances) to a target on Earth's surface?
39.x: LiDAR (Light Detection And Ranging) uses laser pulses to measure distances and make 3D maps.

39.s: The rays that deeply darken the photographic plate are:
39.x: X-rays are highly energetic and strongly expose (darken) photographic plates and film, the basis of radiography; infrared and visible light act weakly. Ultraviolet also affects plates but less deeply.

39.s: Which of the following radiation/light has longest wavelength among the given options?
39.src: APPSC 2018 Lecturers in Government Polytechnic Colleges (Eng
39.x: Wavelength falls from radio through microwave, infrared, visible (red to violet), ultraviolet to X-rays, so infrared is the longest here.

39.s: Which of the following can be used to capture the heat radiated by volcanic eruptions?
39.x: Volcanic heat is emitted thermal infrared radiation, so infrared-sensitive sensors capture it; visible or UV sensors record reflected light, not heat.

39.s: Which of the following band of Electromagnetic Spectrum is best suited for satellite remote sensing of cloud covered disaster affected area, because of its ability to penetrate clouds?
39.src: APPSC 2021 Medical Officer (Ayurveda) In Ayush Department
39.x: Only long-wave microwave/radio energy (as used by SAR) passes through cloud, so 'Radio' is right. Visible, infrared and near-infrared light are blocked by cloud (official key: Visible, a factual error).

39.s: The colour of light is determined by its
39.x: The colour of light is set by its wavelength (frequency); red is longest and violet shortest in the visible band.

39.s: Which of the following is an active sensor used in remote sensing?
39.x: A laser is an active sensor because it sends its own pulse and reads the echo; visible, infrared and X-ray cameras are passive here.

39.s: Which of the following is not an application of LASER?
39.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Village Agriculture Ass
39.x: LASIK eye surgery, LiDAR and holography all use lasers; MRI uses strong magnets and radio waves.

39.s:
Consider the following statements about SAR sensors:
1. SAR sensors can observe through clouds and in darkness.
2. SAR is an active sensor that uses its own microwave signal and reads the echo.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
39.x: Both are correct: SAR sends its own microwave signal instead of relying on sunlight, so it works through clouds and in darkness.

39.s: For which of the following is hyperspectral remote sensing particularly useful?
o: Producing radar echoes from a single microwave band
Identifying materials or chemicals using hundreds of narrow spectral bands
Measuring only the revisit interval of a satellite
Determining satellite launch velocity without imaging
39.x: Hyperspectral sensing uses hundreds of narrow spectral bands, enabling identification of materials and their chemical characteristics.
39.tq: Link the prefix ‘hyper’ with numerous narrow bands and material discrimination.
xs: Hyperspectral sensing uses **hundreds of narrow bands** for **material/chemical identification** — option **(2)**.
Radar echoes come from **SAR** (active, microwave), not hyperspectral imagers.
xa: Example: DRDO's hyperspectral **EOS-N1 "Anvesha"** — lost on **PSLV-C62** (Jan **2026**).
**HySIS** is ISRO's hyperspectral imaging satellite.
**EOS-05** carries multispectral + hyperspectral imaging (visible to long-wave IR) from GEO.

39.s: Which of the following is a passive remote-sensing instrument?
39.x: Infrared radiometers record emitted heat and are passive; SAR and laser/LiDAR send their own pulse and are active.

39.s: What does optical (visible/near-infrared) imaging need?
39.x: Optical sensors use reflected light, so they need daylight and a clear sky, unlike SAR.

39.s: Which one of the following is an example of an active remote-sensing system?
39.x: LiDAR sends its own laser pulse and reads the echo, so it is active (APPSC 2023: laser is active). Multispectral cameras, infrared radiometers and visible cameras record sunlight reflected or heat emitted by the target, so they are passive.
39.tq: Own pulse + echo = active: RISAT SAR, LiDAR.
xs: **Laser-based LiDAR** is **active** — it sends its own pulse and reads the echo — option **(3)** (APPSC **2023**).
**Multispectral cameras**, **infrared radiometers** and **visible cameras** are **passive** — they record sunlight or emitted heat.
xa: Another active system: **RISAT radar (SAR)**.
LiDAR maps **elevation, 3D terrain and forest canopy height**.
Resourcesat and Oceansat are passive systems.

39.s: Which of the following has the shortest wavelength?
39.x: In the electromagnetic spectrum, wavelength falls from infrared to visible to ultraviolet to gamma rays, so gamma rays have the shortest wavelength.

39.s: Which technique is most directly suited to detecting heat from volcanic eruptions, forest fires and urban heat?
39.x: Thermal infrared sensing records emitted heat and is therefore useful for volcanic eruptions, forest fires and urban heat mapping.
39.tq: Link emitted heat with thermal infrared and eliminate techniques measuring vegetation, elevation or deformation.
xs: **Thermal infrared** records **emitted heat** — **volcanic eruptions**, forest fires, urban heat — option **(4)**.
APPSC **2023** asked about **infrared-sensitive sensors** for volcanic eruptions.
**NDVI**, **LiDAR** and **InSAR** map vegetation, elevation and deformation respectively.
xa: Forest-fire monitoring is a national use (**INFFRAS**).
**EOS-05** sensors span visible, near-IR, **short-wave IR** and **long-wave IR**.
Infrared radiometers are **passive** sensors.

39.s: ____ resolution refers to how often a remote sensing platform can provide coverage of an area.
39.x: Temporal resolution is how often a satellite revisits (covers) the same area; spatial is the smallest object seen, radiometric the sensitivity to energy differences.

39.s: A number of 52,785 forest fires were detected using MODIS sensor in forest fire season from November 2020 to June 2021. What is the full form of MODIS?
39.x: MODIS = Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectro-radiometer, the NASA sensor that detected 52,785 forest fires in 2020-21.

39.s:
For the measurement/estimation of which of the following are satellite images/ remote sensing data used?

I. Chlorophyll content in the vegetation of a specific location.

II. Greenhouse gas emission from rice paddies of a specific location.

III. Land surface temperature of a specific location.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
39.x: Satellite data estimate chlorophyll (NDVI), land surface temperature (thermal infrared) and methane/GHG emissions from rice paddies, so all three are correct.

39.s:
Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI), Satellite Laser Ranging (SLR) and the Global Positioning System (GPS) are most commonly used space-based techniques for monitoring which of the following?

A. Mapping of flood inundations

B. Near real time depiction of cyclone track

C. Movement of tectonic plates
39.src: APPSC Endowment Executive Officer Grade-III Paper-I 2023
39.x: VLBI, SLR and GPS are space geodesy techniques that measure millimetre shifts of ground stations, i.e. the movement of tectonic plates; floods and cyclones are mapped by imaging satellites.

39.s: Which of the following is not a type of remote sensing resolution ?
39.x: The four resolutions are spatial, spectral, temporal and radiometric; 'chemical' resolution does not exist.

39.s: How many types of resolution are there in remote sensing?
39.x: The four types are spatial, spectral, temporal and radiometric; 'chemical resolution' does not exist.

39.s: In remote sensing, what does temporal resolution refer to?
o: The smallest object a sensor can see
The number and width of spectral bands
How often a satellite revisits the same place
The sensitivity to small differences in energy
39.x: Temporal resolution is the revisit time of a satellite over one place; the other three describe spatial, spectral and radiometric resolution.

39.s: Which of the following remote-sensing technique pairs is correctly matched?
o: InSAR – Elevation and canopy height by laser ranging
LiDAR – Ground deformation such as subsidence
NDVI – Vegetation health from red vs near-infrared reflectance
LiDAR – Vegetation health from red vs near-infrared reflectance
39.x: NDVI gauges vegetation health from red vs NIR reflectance; InSAR maps ground deformation and LiDAR uses laser ranging for elevation and canopy height.
xa: **Thermal infrared** records emitted heat — **volcanic eruptions** (APPSC 2023), forest fires, urban heat.
The four resolution types: **spatial, spectral, temporal, radiometric**.
⚠ "**Chemical**" resolution does not exist (APPSC 2025).

39.s: Which remote-sensing technique maps ground deformation such as land subsidence?
39.x: InSAR maps ground deformation such as subsidence and earthquake or volcano uplift.

39.s: What is LiDAR mainly used to map?
39.x: LiDAR is laser ranging that maps elevation, 3D terrain and canopy height.

39.s: NDVI estimates vegetation health from reflectance in which bands?
39.x: NDVI compares red and near-infrared reflectance to judge vegetation health.

39.s: Which sensor detected 52,785 forest fires in India between November 2020 and June 2021?
39.x: MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectro-radiometer) detected 52,785 forest fires in the 2020-21 fire season.

39.s: An artificial satellite orbiting around the Earth does not fall down. This is so because the attraction of Earth
o: does not exist at such distance
is neutralized by the attraction of the moon
provides the necessary speed for its steady motion
provides the necessary acceleration for its motion
39.x: Earth's gravity supplies the centripetal acceleration that keeps the satellite curving round the Earth; gravity still exists there and the Moon does not cancel it.

39.s:
Satellites used for telecommunication relay are kept in a geostationary orbit. A satellite is said to be in such an orbit when:
1. The orbit is geosynchronous.
2. The orbit is circular.
3. The orbit lies in the plane of the Earth's equator.
4. The orbit is at an altitude of 22,236 km. Which is the correct answer using the code given below:
39.x: A geostationary orbit is geosynchronous, circular and in the equatorial plane (1, 2, 3). Its height is about 35,786 km (22,236 miles), so statement 4 in km is wrong.

39.s:
The satellite used for telecommunication relay are kept in a geostationary orbit. A satellite is said to be in such an orbit when
1. The orbit is geosynchronous.
2. The orbit is circular.
3. The orbit lies in the plane of the Earth's equator.
4. The orbit is at an altitude of 22,236 km.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below
39.x: A geostationary orbit must be geosynchronous, circular and equatorial; its altitude is about 35,786 km, which is 22,236 miles, not 22,236 km.

39.s: What is the typical altitude of a sun-synchronous polar orbit?
39.x: SSOs are near-polar at about 500-900 km, passing a place at the same local solar time for uniform lighting.
xa: **PSLV** was built for this: ~**1,600 kg** to **620 km SSO**.
**MEO** (**2,000-30,000 km**) is used for navigation (**GPS**).
GEO and GSO both have a period of about **23 h 56 min**; geostationary has **zero inclination**.

39.s: GEO and GSO satellites share an orbital period of one sidereal day. About how long is it?
39.x: One sidereal day is about 23 h 56 min; only the geostationary case appears fixed in the sky.
xa: NavIC's **4** inclined satellites are in GSO.
MEO (**2,000-30,000 km**) is used for **GPS** navigation.
GEO is used for **communication and weather**.

39.s: Compared with geosynchronous imagers, what do LEO imaging satellites generally provide?
o: The same detail and revisit frequency
Coarser detail with very frequent observation
39.x: LEO gives finer detail but revisits periodically; geosynchronous imagers give coarser detail but observe priority targets very frequently.
xa: LEO spans **200-2,000 km**; GEO is **35,786 km** over the Equator.
EOS-05 was launched on **GSLV-F17** on **4 Sep 2026**.
India's earlier geostationary "eyes" were weather satellites (**INSAT-3D** series).

39.s: Which orbit is correctly matched with its typical use?
o: SSPO – Satellite appears fixed over the Equator
39.x: LEO extends from about 200 to 2,000 km and is widely used for Earth observation. MEO is used for navigation, GEO for communication and weather, and SSPO for polar imaging.
xa: LEO also hosts the **ISS** and **Starlink-type** constellations.
GEO satellites appear **fixed** — used for communication and weather.
GSO: same altitude, inclined/elliptical → traces a **figure-8**.

39.s: In satellite orbits, what is the full form of LEO?
39.x: LEO is Low Earth Orbit (200-2,000 km), used for Earth observation.

39.s: Why do most Earth-observation satellites use a sun-synchronous orbit?
o: Passes each place at the same local solar time
Lies in the plane of the equator
Keeps the satellite fixed over one longitude
39.x: A sun-synchronous orbit crosses each place at the same local solar time, giving even lighting.

39.s: By what other name is the geostationary orbit known?
39.x: The geostationary orbit, circular and in the equatorial plane, is also called Clarke's orbit.

39.s: Navigation satellites such as GPS mainly use which orbit?
39.x: MEO (2,000-30,000 km) is used for navigation such as GPS.

39.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the geostationary orbit?
o: It lies in the plane of the equator
It traces a figure-8 over the Earth
39.x: A geostationary orbit is circular, equatorial and has zero inclination; the figure-8 is traced by inclined geosynchronous orbits.

39.s: Which one is India's first operational Remote Sensing Satellite?
39.x: IRS-1A (1988) was India's first operational remote-sensing satellite; INSAT-1A and GSAT-1 are communication satellites and PSLV-D3 a rocket.

39.s: India's first Remote Sensing Satellite (IRS-1A) was launched from
39.x: IRS-1A was launched on 17 March 1988 by a Soviet Vostok rocket from Baikonur Cosmodrome, not from Sriharikota.

39.s:
In which of the following activities are Indian Remote Sensing (IRS) satellites used?
1. Assessment of crop productivity
2. Locating groundwater resources
3. Mineral exploration
4. Telecommunications
5. Traffic studies
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
39.x: IRS satellites serve crop productivity, groundwater and mineral exploration; telecommunications is done by INSAT/GSAT and traffic studies are not an IRS function.

39.s: Which one of the following is not a space satellite?
39.x: SLV-3 is a launch vehicle, not a satellite; RS-D1 (Rohini), IRS-1D and INSAT-2D are satellites.

39.s:
In which of the following activities are Indian Remote Sensing (IRS) satellites used?

I. Assessment of crop productivity

II. Locating groundwater resources

III. Mineral exploration

IV. Telecommunications

V. Traffic studies
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
o: I, II, III, IV and V
39.x: IRS satellites are used for crop productivity, groundwater and mineral exploration (I, II, III), not telecommunications or traffic studies.

39.s: India’s first remote sensing satellite (I.R.S.-IA) was launched from :
39.x: IRS-1A was launched on 17 March 1988 from Baikonur (USSR) on a Vostok rocket.

39.s: Which was the first IRS satellite launched on PSLV from Sriharikota?
39.x: IRS-P2 (1994) was the first on PSLV; IRS-1A, 1B and 1C were launched from Baikonur on Soviet rockets.
xa: IRS-1A flew on a Soviet **Vostok** launcher; **IRS-1B** in **1991**.
Precursors: experimental **Bhaskara-1 and Bhaskara-2**.
The IRS programme is the **largest civilian remote-sensing constellation** in the world.

39.s: With which satellite did India's IRS programme, the world's largest civilian remote-sensing constellation, begin in 1988?
39.x: The IRS programme began with IRS-1A in 1988 and is regarded as the largest civilian remote-sensing constellation in the world.
xa: Precursors: **Bhaskara-1 and Bhaskara-2**.
**EOS** is the new naming for all EO satellites.
IRS data are processed at **NRSC, Hyderabad** and shared via **Bhuvan**.

39.s: On which rocket was IRS-1A launched in 1988?
39.x: IRS-1A went up from Baikonur on a Soviet Vostok rocket; IRS-P2 (1994) was the first IRS on PSLV.

39.s: Which was India's first experimental Earth-observation satellite (1979)?
39.x: Bhaskara I (1979) was the first experimental EO satellite; IRS-1A (1988) was the first operational one.

39.s: For which of the following are IRS satellites NOT used?
39.x: IRS data serve crops, groundwater and mineral exploration, not telecommunication.

39.s: Which launch vehicle placed the Rohini satellite in orbit in 1980?
39.x: Rohini was launched in 1980 on India's SLV-3, which is a launch vehicle, not a satellite.

39.s:
Match the following:
List-I:
A. GAGAN
B. GSAT
C. Cartosat
D. Mangalyaan
List-II:
1. Communication
2. Earth observation
3. Traces of methane
4. Navigation
Choose the correct pairs/answer:
39.x: GAGAN – navigation, GSAT – communication, Cartosat – Earth observation, Mangalyaan – traces of methane (its methane sensor).

39.s:
Consider the following statements:

A. Cartosat is used for city mapping

B. RISAT is a microwave satellite

C. SARAL has a thermometer for ocean applications

D. IMS-1 has a scatterometer
Which of the following statements is/are correct:
39.x: Cartosat maps cities (A) and RISAT is a microwave radar satellite (B). SARAL carries the AltiKa altimeter, not a thermometer, and IMS-1 carried cameras, not a scatterometer, so only A and B.

39.s: In July 2021, ISRO announced the launch of its geo-imaging satellite that will enable near-real time monitoring of natural disasters, such as floods and cyclones. The name of this satellite is:
39.x: EOS-03 (earlier GISAT-1) was the geo-imaging satellite for near-real-time flood and cyclone watch; EOS-04 is RISAT-1A, EOS-05 GISAT-1A and EOS-06 Oceansat-3.

39.s: ScatSat is for —
39.x: SCATSAT-1's scatterometer gives ocean wind vectors for weather forecasting and cyclone tracking; it is not for communication, navigation or crops.

39.s: Recently, ISRO and CNES signed an agreement to set up a joint maritime surveillance system. CNES is a space agency of which country?
39.x: CNES (Centre National d'Etudes Spatiales) is France's space agency; ISRO and CNES signed the maritime surveillance pact in March 2019.

39.s: Recently launched Oceansat - II Satellite through
39.x: Oceansat-2 was launched in 2009 on PSLV-C14 from Sriharikota.

39.s: What was the former name of EOS-05, launched by GSLV-F17 on 4 September 2026?
39.x: EOS-05 was formerly GISAT-1A and became the first EO imager working from geosynchronous orbit; GISAT-1 was EOS-03.
xa: Mass **2,367 kg**; multispectral + hyperspectral imaging from visible to **long-wave IR**.
It images priority targets every **5 min** and all of India every **30 min**.
⚠ APPSC **2021** called **EOS-03** the geo-imaging satellite — it was lost at launch.

39.s: Data from which satellite series is mainly used for Potential Fishing Zone (PFZ) advisories?
39.x: Oceansat supports PFZ advisories; Resourcesat serves crops and watersheds, Cartosat mapping and RISAT SAR imaging.
xa: **Cartosat-3** gives ~**25 cm** imagery.
**EOS-04 (RISAT-1A)** SAR fed NRSC's **CROP** wheat estimate; **EOS-06 (Oceansat-3)** gives PFZ advisories.
**SARAL** is an **ISRO-CNES** altimetry satellite; **HySIS** is **hyperspectral**.

39.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Oceansat — ocean colour and sea-surface temperature
39.x: HySIS is a hyperspectral-imaging satellite. Direct-to-home broadcasting is associated with communication satellites, not HySIS.
39.tq: Find the mismatched application by separating EO functions from communication functions.
xs: **HySIS — DTH broadcasting** is wrong — option **(4)**; HySIS does **hyperspectral imaging**, and DTH is a **GSAT** service.
The others are right: **SCATSAT-1** – ocean wind vectors; **RISAT** – all-weather, day-night SAR; **Oceansat** – ocean colour, sea-surface temperature.
xa: SCATSAT-1 also supports **cyclone forecasting**.
**SARAL** (ISRO-CNES) measures **sea-surface height** with the **AltiKa Ka-band** altimeter.
Oceansat supports **Potential Fishing Zone** advisories.

39.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: SARAL — hyperspectral imaging of agricultural fields
39.x: SARAL is an ISRO-CNES altimetry mission using the AltiKa Ka-band altimeter to measure sea-surface height; hyperspectral agricultural imaging is associated with HySIS.
39.tq: Find the single application belonging to another satellite series.
xs: **SARAL — hyperspectral imaging of agricultural fields** is wrong — option **(3)**; hyperspectral imaging is **HySIS**.
**SARAL** is an **ISRO-CNES** altimetry mission measuring **sea-surface height** with the **AltiKa Ka-band** altimeter.
xa: CNES is the French partner.
**SCATSAT-1** measures ocean-surface **wind vectors**.
**Oceansat** measures ocean colour and **sea-surface temperature**.

39.s: For what purpose was EOS-03, also known as GISAT-1, mainly intended?
o: Near-real-time geo-imaging of floods and cyclones
Measuring ocean winds for cyclone forecasting
39.x: EOS-03, formerly GISAT-1, was designed for geo-imaging and near-real-time observation of events such as floods and cyclones.
39.tq: Separate the intended mission application from the later launch outcome.
xs: **EOS-03 (GISAT-1)** was meant for **near-real-time geo-imaging of floods and cyclones** from geostationary orbit — option **(2)** (APPSC **2021** PYQ).
It was **lost** on **GSLV-F10** in **Aug 2021** (cryogenic stage failure).
xa: **SCATSAT-1** measures ocean winds; **SARAL** carries the **Ka-band** altimeter.
EOS-05 images all of India every **30 min**.

39.s: EOS-06 is the new name of which satellite?
39.x: EOS-06 is Oceansat-3 (used for PFZ advisories); EOS-04 is RISAT-1A.
xa: EOS-06 supplies **PFZ** fishing advisories (Apr **2026**).
**CROP** = Comprehensive Remote Sensing Observation on Crop Progress — tracks sowing, growth, harvest.
**EOS-08** is a microsatellite on **SSLV-D3** (**2024**).

39.s: A problem in which stage caused the failure of EOS-03 (GISAT-1), launched by GSLV-F10 in August 2021?
39.x: The EOS-03 mission failed due to a cryogenic-stage problem.
xa: It was meant for near-real-time **floods/cyclones** monitoring (APPSC **2021** PYQ).
Its successor **EOS-05 (GISAT-1A)** succeeded on **GSLV-F17** (**4 Sep 2026**).

39.s: What does SCATSAT-1 measure with its scatterometer?
39.x: SCATSAT-1's scatterometer measures ocean wind vectors and helps track cyclones.

39.s: SARAL, carrying the AltiKa Ka-band altimeter, is a joint satellite of ISRO and which agency?
39.x: SARAL is an ISRO-CNES (France) satellite measuring sea-surface height.

39.s: EOS-04 is the new name of which satellite?
39.x: EOS-04 was RISAT-1A, a SAR satellite; GISAT-1 became EOS-03 and Oceansat-3 became EOS-06.

39.s: For what are Resourcesat satellites mainly used?
39.x: Resourcesat is for crops; Cartosat maps, Oceansat gives PFZ advisories and RISAT does radar imaging.

39.s:
Which of the following statements about NISAR are correct?

A. It is an Earth-Observation satellite, jointly developed by the NASA and ISRO

B. It was envisioned by NASA and ISRO eight years ago in 2014.

C. It is expected to be launched in January 2024 from Satish Dhawan Space Centre.

D. It is a High Earth Orbit (HEO) observatory and will operate for a minimum of ten years.
Choose the correct answer:
39.x:
'expected to be launched in January 2024' — now launched 30 July 2025 on GSLV-F16 from Sriharikota into a sun-synchronous orbit and operational (PMF S&T Part 2 p.56)
A, B and C were correct when asked: NISAR is a NASA-ISRO Earth-observation radar satellite, agreed in 2014, then due from Sriharikota in Jan 2024 (now launched 30 July 2025 on GSLV-F16). D is wrong: it flies in a sun-synchronous low Earth orbit.

39.s: Which of the following satellite missions, a collaboration between NASA and ISRO, is set to launch in June 2025?
39.src: APPSC 2023 Lecturers in Government Degree Colleges
39.x:
'set to launch in June 2025' — now launched 30 July 2025 on GSLV-F16 and operational (PMF S&T Part 2 p.56)
NISAR is the NASA-ISRO SAR mission (NASA L-band, ISRO S-band); the others are Indian-only satellites. It actually launched on 30 July 2025 on GSLV-F16 (now operational).

39.s: In which band does the radar provided by ISRO for NISAR operate?
39.x: ISRO gives the S-band and NASA the L-band radar; NISAR was launched by GSLV-F16 on 30 July 2025.
xa: NISAR is the world's first **dual-frequency radar** satellite.
**EOS-09** (C-band SAR) was lost on **PSLV-C61** (May 2025).
DRDO's hyperspectral **EOS-N1 "Anvesha"** was lost on **PSLV-C62** (Jan 2026).

39.s: Which of the following applications is NOT associated with EOS-05?
39.x: EOS-05 is intended for applications such as floods, cyclones, forest fires, crops and security. Deep-sea submarine communication is not listed among its applications.
39.tq: Find the option outside the satellite's Earth-imaging application set.
xs: **Deep-sea submarine communication** is NOT an EOS-05 application — option **(2)**.
EOS-05 serves **floods, cyclones, forest fires, crops and security**.
xa: Multispectral + hyperspectral imaging (visible to **long-wave IR**) from GEO.
It images priority targets every **5 min** and all of India every **30 min**.

39.s: On which launch vehicle was EOS-N1 'Anvesha', DRDO's hyperspectral satellite, lost in January 2026?
39.x: EOS-N1 failed on PSLV-C62 (Jan 2026); EOS-09 was lost on PSLV-C61 (May 2025).
xa: **EOS-03 (GISAT-1)** was lost on **GSLV-F10** in **Aug 2021**.
Hyperspectral = **hundreds of narrow bands** → material/chemical identification.
**EOS-04 (RISAT-1A)** is the working SAR satellite used for **CROP**.

39.s: Which launch vehicle launched NISAR on 30 July 2025?
39.x: NISAR flew on GSLV-F16, not on a PSLV.

39.s: NISAR is the world's first satellite of which type?
39.x: NISAR, with NASA L-band and ISRO S-band radars and a 12 m reflector, is the first dual-frequency radar satellite.

39.s: On which launch vehicle was EOS-09, a C-band SAR satellite, lost in May 2025?
39.x: PSLV-C61 lost EOS-09 in May 2025; PSLV-C62 lost EOS-N1 and GSLV-F10 lost EOS-03.

39.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about EOS-05?
o: It images from visible to long-wave infrared
39.x: EOS-05 was launched by GSLV-F17 from Sriharikota; the other statements are correct.

39.s: What is the size of the antenna reflector of NISAR?
39.x: NISAR carries a 12 m antenna reflector for its L-band and S-band radars.

39.s: ScatSat is for
39.x: SCATSAT-1 (2016) carries a Ku-band scatterometer measuring ocean-surface winds, so it is for weather monitoring and cyclone forecasting, not communication or education.

39.s: ____ is a satellite that provides weather forecasting, cyclone prediction and tracking services to India.
39.x: SCATSAT-1's scatterometer gives ocean wind data for weather forecasting and cyclone prediction and tracking. GSAT-31 and GSAT-7A are communication satellites, and Cartosat-2C does mapping.

39.s: ____ is a collaboration between five federal agencies that are major users and producers of satellite land remote sensing data.
39.x: JACIE (Joint Agency Commercial Imagery Evaluation) is a collaboration of US agencies (NASA, NOAA, NGA, USGS, USDA) that use and produce satellite land remote-sensing data; the other options are Indian institutes.

39.s: For the purpose of effective utilization of remote sensing and GIS technology, a web geo-portal has been developed by National Informatics Centre (NIC), initially for the use of National Capital Region (NCR). What is this geo-portal called as?
39.x: PARIMAN (Portal for Analytical Regional Information and Mapping of NCR) is the NIC-developed web geo-portal of the NCR Planning Board, launched in 2021 and opened to the public in July 2022.

39.s: What is the name of the web based Geo Portal developed by ISRO and made available for public use?
39.src: Royalty Inspector, Agriculture Officers, Town Planning Asst.
39.x: Bhuvan is ISRO's web-based geoportal giving open satellite data to the public; GAGAN is navigation.

39.s: The earliest satellite images that revealed land subsidence affecting the town of Joshimath in Uttarakhand, released by the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC)-ISRO in January 2023, were taken by the ____ satellite.
39.x: NRSC's January 2023 Joshimath subsidence images came from Cartosat-2S.

39.s: What is the name of the forest fire response and assessment system of India?

39.x: INFFRAS is the Indian Forest Fire Response and Assessment System, an NRSC application.

o: A mini satellite launched by ISRO for promoting distance education in India
The name given to the next Moon Impact Probe for Chandrayaan-II
A geoportal of ISRO with 3-D imaging capabilities of India
A space telescope developed by India
39.x: Bhuvan is ISRO's geoportal with 3-D imaging of India, not a satellite, Moon probe or telescope.

39.x: Resourcesat-2A was launched on PSLV-C36 on 7 December 2016 for resource monitoring.

39.x:

39.s: Where are IIRS and CSSTEAP, which build capacity in space applications, located?
39.x: Both IIRS and CSSTEAP are in Dehradun.

AP's remote-sensing agency is **APSAC**.

xs: SDSC-SHAR contributes data for **Bay of Bengal** cyclone tracking for **APSDMA** — option **(2)**.

xa: SDSC-SHAR lies in **Tirupati district**, AP.
AP's own remote-sensing agency is **APSAC**.
**Bhuvan** cyclone tracks use **RISAT and INSAT-3DS** data.

39.s: SAR data from which satellite is used by NRSC's CROP framework to track crop sowing, growth and harvest?
39.x: CROP uses EOS-04 SAR data near real time; Bhuvan's flood maps and cyclone tracks use RISAT and INSAT-3DS data.

**Yuktdhara** portal helps gram panchayats plan **MGNREGA** assets.
National uses include **FASAL** crop forecasting and drought assessment.

39.s:
Consider the following statements about national Earth-observation applications of NRSC:

39.x: FASAL and INFFRAS are NRSC Earth-observation applications; civil aviation precision landing is the job of GAGAN, not an NRSC application.

39.s: In the Indian remote-sensing data chain, where is the nodal processing centre located?
39.x: After collection and reception at a ground station, remote sensing data are processed at the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), Hyderabad, which functions as the nodal centre.
39.tq: Test the institutional location by distinguishing the processing centre from the launch and headquarters locations.
xs: Data are processed at the nodal **NRSC, Hyderabad** — option **(3)**.
Chain: **data collection** → **ground station** → **processing at NRSC** → supply to ministries, states, disaster agencies.
xa: Data are stored in **Indian data centres** and opened through **NRSC** and the **Bhuvan geoportal**.
Other ISRO platforms: **Bhoonidhi**, **MOSDAC**, **VEDAS** (**2026**).
NRSC released the **Landslide Atlas of India** (**2023**).

39.x: Bhuvan is the ISRO geoportal through which Earth-observation data are made openly accessible along with NRSC data services.

xs: **Bhuvan** is ISRO's **geoportal** for open EO data — option **(4)**.
**Yuktdhara** helps gram panchayats plan **MGNREGA** assets; **INFFRAS** is the forest-fire system; **SIS-DP** is a national use.
xa: Bhuvan gives **flood-inundation maps** and **cyclone tracks** from **RISAT and INSAT-3DS** data (Apr **2026**).
Other ISRO platforms: **Bhoonidhi**, **MOSDAC**, **VEDAS**.
Processing happens at **NRSC, Hyderabad**.

39.x: Joshimath subsidence was mapped with Cartosat-2S images; NRSC also released the Landslide Atlas of India (2023).
xa: **EOS-06 (Oceansat-3)** gives **PFZ** fishing advisories.
**NRSC, Hyderabad** is the nodal data processor; data open through **Bhuvan** geoportal.
Other ISRO platforms: **Bhoonidhi**, **MOSDAC**, **VEDAS**.

39.x: NRSC prepared the Landslide Atlas (2023), runs CROP and mapped Joshimath; CWC monitors glacial lakes.

39.x: The 2023 atlas counted 7,570 glacial lakes in India.

39.x: The Central Water Commission (CWC) monitors glacial lakes with NRSC imagery since 2011.

39.x: The AP Space Applications Centre (APSAC) is the state remote-sensing agency; APSDMA is the disaster agency.

39.x: Bhuvan (ISRO geoportal) and Bhoonidhi are run by NRSC, Hyderabad; MOSDAC and VEDAS are platforms of SAC, Ahmedabad.

39.x: Bhuvan, Bhoonidhi, MOSDAC and VEDAS are ISRO's EO data platforms.

39.x: CWC monitoring with NRSC imagery shows Himalayan glacial lake area rose by about 9% from 2011 to 2025.

39.x: SDSC-SHAR, Sriharikota, is in Tirupati district.

41.s: There is no atmosphere on the surface of the moon because :
o: Escape velocity of gas molecules is less than RMS
41.x: The Moon's gravity is weak, so its escape velocity is lower than the RMS speed of gas molecules; any gas escapes. Distance from Earth, its orbit or sunlight are not the reason.

41.s: There is no atmosphere on the Moon because –
o: It is near to the Earth
It receives light from the Sun
The escape velocity of gas molecules on it is less than
41.x: The Moon's escape velocity is lower than the RMS speed of gas molecules, so gases escape and it keeps no atmosphere.

It will rotate into the orbit of Earth

8 km/s is below Earth's escape velocity of 11.2 km/s, so the object cannot leave Earth's gravity and returns – the key and books follow this.

41.s: What is a Hohmann transfer?

A point of gravitational balance in a two-body system
A direct vertical launch requiring continuous engine thrust
A fuel-efficient transfer between two orbits using an elliptical orbit and two engine burns

xs: A **Hohmann transfer** is a **fuel-efficient elliptical orbit between two orbits** using **two engine burns** — option **(4)**.
**Controlled low-speed touchdown** is a **soft landing**; a **balance point** is a **Lagrange point**.
xa: **Mangalyaan (MOM)** used a Hohmann transfer to reach Mars.
MOM entered Mars orbit on **24 September 2014** — on the **first attempt**.
Escape velocity: **11.2 km/s**.

41.s: In a two-body system, what are the points at which a small object can remain in balance called?
41.x: Lagrange points are five points, L1 to L5, in a two-body system where a small object can remain in balance. The Sun–Earth L1 point is about 1.5 million km sunward of Earth.
41.tq: Match the exact scientific term with its defining condition.
xs: These are **Lagrange points** — option **(2)**.
There are **five** (**L1-L5**) in a two-body system.
**Hohmann transfer** is an orbit-transfer method, not a balance point.
xa: Sun-Earth **L1** is ~**1.5 million km** sunward — **Aditya-L1's** station.
Aditya-L1 sits in a **halo orbit** around L1 → continuous view of the Sun, no eclipse.
Escape velocity of Earth: **11.2 km/s**.

42.s:

IV. The ownership and use of the Space station are intergovernmental established by treaties and agreements.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

Key 'only two' (UPSC official key): Axiom-4 (ISS experiments) and Gaganyaan (crew to conduct microgravity experiments) support microgravity research; SpaDeX is a docking technology demonstration.

42.s: Which of the following agencies jointly operate the International Space Station?

xa: The ISS is a modular microgravity lab in **LEO** (~**400 km**), **continuously inhabited since November 2000**.
